c.title: Phaethon's Puzzle: The Rock That Acts Like a Comet
text: Most of the year's great meteor showers have a well-understood origin. A comet, warmed by the Sun, releases a trail of ice and dust, and when Earth crosses that trail, the particles burn up in our atmosphere. The Geminids, which peak each December, break this pattern, and in doing so they have become one of the more intriguing puzzles in planetary science.

The shower's parent body, 3200 Phaethon, was identified in 1983 in data from the Infrared Astronomical Satellite. Its orbit matched the Geminid stream almost perfectly, but Phaethon showed none of the features of a typical comet: no glowing coma and no long tail of gas. It appeared, by most measures, to be a rocky asteroid roughly five kilometers across.

That raises an obvious question. Asteroids are not supposed to shed enough material to feed a powerful shower. One leading explanation focuses on Phaethon's unusual orbit, which carries it closer to the Sun than Mercury. At that distance its surface may become hot enough to crack, throwing off dust as the rock heats and cools. Spacecraft have recorded a faint tail near its closest approach, but a 2023 study suggested the tail is made largely of sodium gas rather than dust, and the activity seen today appears far too weak to explain the Geminids.

Many researchers therefore suspect that the stream was created by a dramatic event in the past, perhaps a breakup or burst of activity thousands of years ago, and that today's Phaethon is the quiet remnant of a more active body. In that view, Phaethon may be an extinct comet or a rock comet, blurring a line that textbooks usually draw sharply.

Answers may come from DESTINY+, a planned Japanese spacecraft designed to fly past Phaethon and study its dust directly. Until then, the Geminids offer a reminder that categories in science are tools, not laws of nature. When an object refuses to fit, it may be the category, not the object, that needs rethinking.

For observers on the ground, of course, none of this changes the experience. On a dark, clear night in mid-December, the Geminids still streak across the sky by the dozen, fragments of a mystery burning up high above our heads. No telescope is needed to enjoy them, and no theory is needed to be amazed.
tz: 一年中大多數壯觀的流星雨，來源都很清楚：彗星受太陽加熱，釋放出一道冰與塵埃的軌跡，當地球穿過這道軌跡，顆粒就在大氣中燒盡。每年十二月達到極大期的雙子座流星雨卻打破了這個模式，也因此成為行星科學中較引人入勝的謎題之一。
這場流星雨的母體「3200 法厄同」是在 1983 年從紅外線天文衛星的資料中被辨識出來的。它的軌道幾乎與雙子座流星群完全吻合，但法厄同沒有典型彗星的任何特徵：沒有發光的彗髮，也沒有長長的氣體彗尾。依大多數標準來看，它是一顆直徑約五公里的岩質小行星。
這引出一個明顯的問題：小行星照理不會散出足以形成強大流星雨的物質。一個主要的解釋著眼於法厄同不尋常的軌道，它會比水星更接近太陽。在那樣的距離下，它的表面可能熱到裂開，岩石在冷熱交替中拋出塵埃。太空船曾在它最接近太陽時記錄到一條微弱的尾巴，但 2023 年的一項研究指出，這條尾巴主要是鈉氣體而不是塵埃，而且今天觀察到的活動似乎太微弱，遠不足以解釋雙子座流星雨。
因此許多研究者推測，這道流星群是過去一次劇烈事件造成的，也許是數千年前的一次解體或活動爆發，而今天的法厄同只是一個曾經更活躍的天體所留下的安靜殘骸。依這個觀點，法厄同可能是一顆熄滅的彗星，或一顆「岩石彗星」，模糊了教科書通常劃得很清楚的界線。
答案可能來自 DESTINY+，這是一艘日本計畫中的太空船，設計要飛掠法厄同、直接研究它的塵埃。在那之前，雙子座流星雨提醒我們：科學中的分類是工具，不是自然定律。當一個天體不肯被歸類時，需要重新思考的，可能是分類，而不是那個天體。
當然，對地面上的觀測者來說，這些都不會改變觀賞的體驗。在十二月中旬黑暗晴朗的夜晚，雙子座流星仍然成打地劃過天空——那是一個謎團的碎片，在我們頭頂高處燃燒殆盡。欣賞它們不需要望遠鏡，被它們震撼也不需要任何理論。

topic: The Bystander Effect: Why Crowds Don't Always Help
zh: 旁觀者效應：人多為什麼不一定有人幫忙
src: Darley & Latané (1968) · Manning, Levine & Collins (2007) · Fischer et al. (2011) · Philpot et al. (2019)

a.title: Why Nobody Helps
text: Imagine you drop all your books in a busy hallway at school. Many students walk past, but no one stops to help. Are they all unkind? Maybe not. Psychologists call this the bystander effect.
A bystander is a person who sees something happen but is not part of it. The bystander effect means that when many people are around, each person is less likely to help someone in trouble.

In 1968, two American psychologists, John Darley and Bibb Latané, did a famous experiment. Students sat in different rooms and talked over speakers. Suddenly, one student seemed to become very sick, but it was really a recording. When people thought they were the only listener, most of them went to get help quickly. When they thought many others were listening, fewer people helped, and they were slower.
Why does this happen? Each person thinks, "Someone else will do it." People also look at others. If nobody else looks worried, they think everything is OK.
But here is some good news. A study published in 2019 looked at real videos from street cameras. It found that in most fights in public, at least one person stepped in to help.

So what can you do? If you need help in a crowd, point to one person and say, "You in the red jacket, please call 119!" And when you see someone in trouble, don't wait for others. Be the one who helps.
tz: 想像你在學校擁擠的走廊上把書全掉在地上。很多學生走過去，卻沒有人停下來幫忙。他們都很冷漠嗎？不一定。心理學家把這種現象叫做旁觀者效應。
旁觀者是看到事情發生、但不是當事人的人。旁觀者效應指的是：當周圍有很多人時，每個人去幫助遇到麻煩的人的可能性就會變小。
1968 年，兩位美國心理學家約翰・達利和比布・拉塔內做了一個有名的實驗。學生們坐在不同的房間，透過喇叭說話。突然，有一位學生似乎病得很嚴重，但其實那只是錄音。當受試者以為只有自己在聽時，大多數人很快就去找人幫忙；當他們以為還有很多人也在聽時，幫忙的人變少了，而且動作也比較慢。
為什麼會這樣？每個人都在想：「別人會去做的。」人們也會看別人的反應。如果沒有人看起來很擔心，他們就以為一切都沒事。
不過也有好消息。2019 年發表的一項研究分析了街頭監視器拍到的真實影片，發現在大多數公共場所的衝突中，至少有一個人出面幫忙。
那你可以怎麼做？如果你在人群中需要幫助，就指著一個人說：「穿紅外套的你，請打 119！」而當你看到有人遇到麻煩時，不要等別人，當那個出手幫忙的人。

b.title: The Bystander Effect: When Crowds Freeze
text: In March 1964, a young woman named Kitty Genovese was murdered outside her apartment in New York City. Two weeks later, The New York Times reported that 38 neighbors had watched or heard the attack without calling the police. The story shocked the country and inspired psychologists to ask why people sometimes fail to help.

In a series of experiments, John Darley and Bibb Latané found that the presence of others can reduce helping. In one study, participants heard over an intercom what sounded like another student having a seizure. Those who believed they were alone usually went for help; those who believed several others could hear were less likely to act, and slower when they did. In another study, students filling out forms in a room that slowly filled with smoke reported it far less often when they sat with calm strangers than when they were alone.

The researchers proposed two causes. The first is diffusion of responsibility: the more people present, the less each one feels personally responsible. The second is pluralistic ignorance: in an unclear situation, we look to others for clues, and if everyone looks calm, we conclude that nothing is wrong.

The effect is real, but the famous story behind it was exaggerated. Later investigations found that far fewer than 38 people witnessed the attack, few could see clearly what was happening, and at least one neighbor did call the police. Moreover, a 2019 study of street-camera footage from three countries found that in about nine out of ten public conflicts, at least one bystander intervened, and the more bystanders there were, the more likely it was that someone helped.
The lesson, then, is not that people are selfish, but that responsibility can feel shared until someone claims it. Knowing about the effect may itself make you more likely to be the person who acts.
tz: 1964 年 3 月，一位名叫凱蒂・吉諾維斯的年輕女子在紐約市的公寓外遇害。兩週後，《紐約時報》報導有 38 位鄰居目睹或聽到攻擊，卻沒有人報警。這則報導震驚全美，也促使心理學家探究：為什麼人們有時不伸出援手。
在一系列實驗中，約翰・達利和比布・拉塔內發現，他人在場會讓助人行為減少。在一項研究中，受試者透過對講機聽到像是另一位學生癲癇發作的聲音。以為只有自己聽到的人通常會去求援；以為還有好幾個人聽到的人比較不會行動，就算行動也比較慢。在另一項研究中，學生在一間慢慢充滿煙霧的房間裡填表格，當他們和冷靜的陌生人坐在一起時，回報煙霧的比例遠低於獨自一人的時候。
研究者提出兩個原因。第一是責任分散：在場的人越多，每個人覺得自己該負的責任就越少。第二是多數無知：在不明確的情況下，我們會看別人的反應找線索，如果大家看起來都很冷靜，我們就斷定沒什麼問題。
這個效應是真的，但它背後那個有名的故事被誇大了。後來的調查發現，目睹攻擊的人遠少於 38 位，能清楚看到發生什麼事的人很少，而且至少有一位鄰居確實報了警。此外，2019 年一項分析三個國家街頭監視器畫面的研究發現，在大約十分之九的公共衝突中，至少有一位旁觀者出面介入，而且旁觀者越多，有人幫忙的機率越高。
所以，這個教訓並不是人很自私，而是：在有人主動承擔之前，責任會讓人覺得是大家共同的。光是知道這個效應，也許就會讓你更可能成為那個採取行動的人。

c.title: Rethinking the Bystander Effect
text: Few findings in social psychology are as widely known as the bystander effect: the idea that the more people witness an emergency, the less likely any individual is to help. Taught in textbooks for decades, it has also shaped first-aid training, which now tells people in trouble to single out one person, such as "You, in the blue shirt, call an ambulance," rather than shout to a crowd.

The effect grew out of a story. After Kitty Genovese was killed in New York in 1964, a front-page report claimed that 38 respectable, law-abiding citizens had watched and done nothing. Psychologists John Darley and Bibb Latané set out to explain this apparent apathy, and their laboratory studies in 1968 showed that people who believed others were present responded more slowly to emergencies, or not at all.

Decades later, the story itself began to unravel. Researchers who examined court and police records concluded that the number 38 was inflated, that most witnesses had only heard noises or seen part of the attack, and that some had tried to help. In 2016, the newspaper acknowledged that its original account had been flawed. The parable had outlived the facts.

The laboratory findings have proved more durable, but their meaning is debated. A 2011 review of more than a hundred studies, led by Peter Fischer, found that the effect weakens in situations that are clearly dangerous, perhaps because danger is recognized faster and others can offer physical support. And when Richard Philpot and colleagues analyzed street-camera recordings of real public conflicts in three countries, published in 2019, they found that someone intervened in roughly nine out of ten cases. Larger groups made it more, not less, likely that at least one person would act.

These results do not erase the bystander effect so much as reframe it. The chance that any particular individual helps may still drop as a group grows, yet the chance that somebody helps can rise, simply because there are more potential helpers. Which of these matters more depends on the question being asked, and on whether the person in trouble needs one helper or many.

The revised picture is more hopeful, but it is no excuse for passivity. The lessons of first-aid training still hold: name a specific person, state the problem clearly and, if you are the bystander, assume the responsibility is yours.
tz: 在社會心理學中，很少有研究發現像旁觀者效應這樣廣為人知：目睹緊急事件的人越多，任何一個人出手幫忙的可能性就越低。它在教科書裡教了幾十年，也影響了急救訓練——現在的訓練會教遇到危難的人指定一個人，例如「穿藍衣服的你，叫救護車」，而不是對著人群大喊。
這個效應源自一個故事。1964 年凱蒂・吉諾維斯在紐約遇害後，一則頭版報導聲稱有 38 位「體面、守法的市民」在旁觀看卻什麼都沒做。心理學家約翰・達利和比布・拉塔內開始著手解釋這種看似冷漠的現象；他們 1968 年的實驗室研究顯示，以為有其他人在場的人，對緊急狀況的反應比較慢，甚至完全沒有反應。
幾十年後，這個故事本身開始瓦解。查閱法院和警方紀錄的研究者斷定，38 這個數字被灌水了，大多數目擊者只聽到聲音或只看到攻擊的一部分，而且有些人曾試圖幫忙。2016 年，該報承認當初的報導有缺失。這則寓言比事實流傳得更久。
實驗室的發現較經得起考驗，但它的意義仍有爭議。2011 年由彼得・費雪主導、回顧一百多項研究的分析發現，在明顯危險的情況下，這個效應會減弱，也許是因為危險更快被察覺，而且其他人能提供實際的支援。而理查・菲爾波特和同事分析三個國家街頭監視器拍下的真實公共衝突，於 2019 年發表結果，發現大約十件裡有九件有人出面介入。人越多，反而越可能至少有一個人採取行動。
這些結果與其說是推翻了旁觀者效應，不如說是重新詮釋它。隨著人數增加，任何「特定一個人」出手的機率也許仍會下降，但「有人」出手的機率卻可能上升，原因很簡單：可能的幫手變多了。哪一個比較重要，取決於我們問的是什麼問題，也取決於遇到危難的人需要一個幫手還是很多個。
修正後的圖像比較樂觀，但這不是袖手旁觀的藉口。急救訓練的教訓仍然成立：指定特定的人、清楚說明問題，而如果你是旁觀者，就把責任當成是你自己的。

topic: Ada Lovelace: The First Computer Programmer?
zh: 愛達・勒芙蕾絲：第一位電腦程式設計師？
src: Science Museum (London) · British Library · Computer History Museum

a.title: The First Computer Programmer
text: Who wrote the first computer program? Many people say it was a woman named Ada Lovelace. Amazingly, she did it more than 180 years ago, long before any computers were built.

Ada was born in London on December 10, 1815. Her father was the famous poet Lord Byron, but she never really knew him. Her mother loved math, and she made sure Ada studied math and science from a young age.

When Ada was 17, she met an inventor named Charles Babbage. He was planning a machine called the Analytical Engine. It could do math by itself, step by step. Ada was very interested in it, and the two became good friends.

In 1843, Ada translated an article about the machine from French into English. She added her own notes, and they were much longer than the article! In one note, she wrote a list of steps for the machine to follow. Many people call this the first computer program.
Ada also had a big idea. She believed machines like this could one day do more than math. For example, they might make music. Today, computers really do make music, draw pictures and much more.

Sadly, Babbage never finished his machine, and Ada died when she was only 36. But her ideas lived on. Today, a computer language is named Ada after her, and people around the world remember her as a pioneer.
tz: 第一個電腦程式是誰寫的？很多人說是一位名叫愛達・勒芙蕾絲的女性。令人驚訝的是，她在 180 多年前就做到了，那時候根本還沒有任何電腦。
愛達 1815 年 12 月 10 日出生於倫敦。她的父親是著名詩人拜倫勳爵，但她幾乎不認識他。她的母親熱愛數學，確保愛達從小就學習數學和科學。
愛達 17 歲時認識了一位名叫查爾斯・巴貝奇的發明家。他正在規劃一台叫做「分析機」的機器，它能自己一步一步地做數學運算。愛達對它非常感興趣，兩人也成了好朋友。
1843 年，愛達把一篇介紹這台機器的文章從法文翻譯成英文。她加上了自己的筆記，而筆記比原文還長得多！在其中一則筆記裡，她寫下一連串讓機器照著執行的步驟。很多人把這稱為第一個電腦程式。
愛達還有一個遠大的想法。她相信這樣的機器有一天能做的不只是數學，例如可能會創作音樂。今天，電腦真的能作曲、畫圖，還能做更多事。
可惜的是，巴貝奇從未完成他的機器，而愛達只活到 36 歲。但她的想法流傳了下來。今天有一種電腦語言以她的名字命名為 Ada，世界各地的人都記得她是一位先驅。

b.title: Ada Lovelace: Poetry, Numbers and the First Program
text: Augusta Ada Byron, later the Countess of Lovelace, was born in London on December 10, 1815. Her father, the poet Lord Byron, left England when she was a baby. Her mother, who feared that Ada might inherit his wild temperament, insisted on a strict education in mathematics and science.

At 17, Ada met the mathematician and inventor Charles Babbage and became fascinated by his designs. His proposed Analytical Engine was a mechanical, general-purpose calculator. It would take instructions from punched cards, store numbers in a kind of memory and make decisions based on its results, features that modern computers still share. Building it with the metal parts of the 1800s, however, would have been extremely difficult and expensive.

In 1843, Ada translated an Italian engineer's article about the engine, which had been written in French, and added a series of notes nearly three times as long as the original. In the final note, known as Note G, she set out a step-by-step method for the engine to calculate a series of numbers called the Bernoulli numbers. Because of this, she is often called the first computer programmer. Her program could not be tested, however, because the machine did not exist.

Some historians question that title. They point out that Babbage had already sketched programs for his machine years earlier, and they argue that Ada's mathematical skills have been exaggerated. Others reply that her real achievement lay elsewhere: she saw that the engine could manipulate any symbols, not only numbers, and might one day compose music. Babbage, they note, focused mainly on calculation.

The engine was never built, and Ada died in 1852 at the age of 36. Yet her vision of what she called poetical science, combining imagination with logic, feels strikingly modern. Today, a programming language bears her name, and Ada Lovelace Day celebrates women in science, technology, engineering and math every October.
tz: 奧古斯塔・愛達・拜倫，後來的勒芙蕾絲伯爵夫人，1815 年 12 月 10 日生於倫敦。她的父親、詩人拜倫勳爵在她還是嬰兒時就離開了英國。她的母親擔心愛達會遺傳到父親狂放的性情，堅持讓她接受嚴格的數學與科學教育。
17 歲時，愛達認識了數學家兼發明家查爾斯・巴貝奇，並對他的設計深深著迷。他提出的分析機是一台機械式的通用計算機：它會從打孔卡讀取指令、把數字存放在一種「記憶體」裡，並根據運算結果做出判斷——這些特點至今仍是現代電腦共有的。然而，要用 19 世紀的金屬零件把它造出來，會極為困難又昂貴。
1843 年，愛達翻譯了一位義大利工程師以法文寫成、介紹這台機器的文章，並加上一系列筆記，長度將近原文的三倍。在最後一則被稱為「筆記 G」的筆記中，她提出一套讓機器一步步計算「白努利數」的方法。因此，她常被稱為第一位電腦程式設計師。不過，她的程式無法實際測試，因為這台機器並不存在。
有些歷史學家質疑這個頭銜。他們指出，巴貝奇早在幾年前就已草擬過這台機器的程式，並認為愛達的數學能力被誇大了。另一些人則回應，她真正的成就在別處：她看出這台機器可以處理任何符號，而不只是數字，有一天甚至可能作曲。他們也指出，巴貝奇主要專注在計算上。
這台機器從未被造出來，愛達在 1852 年過世，年僅 36 歲。然而，她所說的「詩意的科學」——結合想像力與邏輯——這個願景至今看來驚人地現代。今天有一種程式語言以她命名，而每年十月的「愛達・勒芙蕾絲日」則表揚在科學、科技、工程與數學領域的女性。

c.title: Beyond Numbers: Ada Lovelace's Poetical Science
text: Discussions of Ada Lovelace tend to swing between two extremes. In one version, she is the lone genius who invented programming a century before electronic computers existed; in the other, she is a well-connected aristocrat whose reputation was inflated by later admirers. The historical record supports neither caricature, and the truth is more interesting than both.

Born on December 10, 1815, Lovelace received an unusually rigorous education for a woman of her era, partly because her mother hoped mathematics would discipline the poetic tendencies associated with Lord Byron. In 1833 she met Charles Babbage, whose Difference Engine was a celebrated, if unfinished, project. His later design, the Analytical Engine, went further: it separated the store, where numbers were held, from the mill, where operations were carried out, and it could repeat steps and branch depending on results.

Lovelace's famous contribution was a set of notes appended to her 1843 translation of an article by the Italian engineer Luigi Menabrea. The notes included a detailed table showing how the engine could calculate Bernoulli numbers, the work most often cited as the first published computer program. Critics point out that Babbage had drafted similar sequences earlier and advised her on the mathematics; their letters show a genuine collaboration rather than a solo invention.

What sets Lovelace apart is not the table but the vision surrounding it. She argued that the engine could act on any objects whose relationships could be expressed in symbols, and speculated that it might compose elaborate pieces of music. At the same time, she cautioned that the engine could not originate anything; it could only do what it was ordered to do. More than a century later, Alan Turing devoted a section of a famous 1950 paper to what he called Lady Lovelace's objection, a debate that continues in arguments about whether AI can be truly creative.

Lovelace died of cancer in 1852, aged 36, and the engine was never built. Her reputation was revived in the twentieth century after a long period of neglect, and in 1980 a programming language was named Ada in her honor.

Seen clearly, her legacy lies less in being first than in asking the right questions: what a general-purpose machine is, what it might do beyond arithmetic, and where its limits lie. Those questions remain open today.
tz: 關於愛達・勒芙蕾絲的討論，往往在兩個極端之間擺盪。一種說法把她描繪成在電子電腦出現前一百年就發明了程式設計的孤獨天才；另一種說法則認為她是人脈很廣的貴族，名聲被後來的仰慕者灌水。歷史紀錄並不支持這兩種誇張的形象，而真相比兩者都更有趣。
勒芙蕾絲生於 1815 年 12 月 10 日，接受了以她那個年代的女性而言極為嚴格的教育，部分原因是她的母親希望數學能約束她身上與拜倫勳爵相連的「詩人」傾向。1833 年，她認識了查爾斯・巴貝奇，他的差分機是一個備受讚譽、但未完成的計畫。他後來設計的分析機更進一步：它把存放數字的「儲存器」和執行運算的「運算器」分開，還能重複步驟，並依結果走向不同的分支。
勒芙蕾絲著名的貢獻，是她 1843 年翻譯義大利工程師路易吉・梅納布雷亞的文章時所附的一組筆記。筆記中有一張詳細的表格，說明這台機器如何計算白努利數——這正是最常被引用為「第一個發表的電腦程式」的作品。批評者指出，巴貝奇更早就草擬過類似的運算步驟，也在數學上給過她建議；他們的書信顯示這是真正的合作，而不是個人的發明。
讓勒芙蕾絲與眾不同的不是那張表格，而是圍繞著它的遠見。她主張，任何能用符號表達彼此關係的事物，這台機器都能處理，並推測它也許能創作精緻的音樂。同時她也提醒，這台機器不能「原創」任何東西，只能做人們命令它做的事。一百多年後，艾倫・圖靈在 1950 年一篇著名的論文中用了一節討論他所謂的「勒芙蕾絲夫人的反對意見」，這場辯論延續到今天關於 AI 能否真正具有創造力的爭論。
勒芙蕾絲在 1852 年因癌症過世，享年 36 歲，那台機器也從未被造出來。她的名聲在長期被忽略之後，於二十世紀重新受到重視，1980 年還有一種程式語言以她命名為 Ada。
看清楚來說，她的遺產與其說在於「第一」，不如說在於問對了問題：通用機器是什麼、它在算術之外還能做什麼、它的極限在哪裡。這些問題到今天仍沒有定論。

a.title: Notice: A Hike for Mountain Day
text: NOTICE: Mountain Club Hike for International Mountain Day

December 11 is International Mountain Day. To celebrate it, the Green Hill Junior High School Mountain Club is planning a one-day hike. All students are welcome, and you don't need to be a club member to join us!

Date: Saturday, December 19. Meeting place: the school gate at 6:00 a.m. Return: about 7:00 p.m. Place: Hehuanshan, Nantou. Cost: NT$600, for the bus and lunch. Sign up in Room 203 before Friday, December 18.
What to bring: a warm jacket, a hat and gloves, a water bottle, a raincoat and some snacks. It can be below 5°C on the mountain in December, even when it is warm in the city.

Rules: Stay on the trail. Take all your trash home with you. Don't feed the animals. If you feel sick or very tired, tell a teacher right away. The air is thin up high, so walk slowly and take breaks.
Why do mountains matter? They give us clean water, and many plants and animals live only there. Let's enjoy the mountain and keep it clean for the next visitors!
tz: 公告：登山社「國際山岳日」健行活動
12 月 11 日是國際山岳日。為了慶祝，綠丘國中登山社規劃了一日健行。歡迎所有同學參加，不是社員也可以加入我們！
日期：12 月 19 日星期六。集合地點：早上 6:00 校門口。回程：大約晚上 7:00。地點：南投合歡山。費用：新台幣 600 元，含車資和午餐。請在 12 月 18 日星期五前到 203 教室報名。
要帶的東西：保暖外套、帽子和手套、水壺、雨衣和一些點心。十二月時山上可能低於攝氏 5 度，就算市區很溫暖也一樣。
規定：走在步道上，不要離開步道。所有垃圾都要帶回家。不要餵食動物。如果覺得不舒服或很累，要馬上告訴老師。高山上空氣稀薄，所以要慢慢走、適時休息。
山為什麼重要？山給我們乾淨的水，而且很多植物和動物只住在那裡。讓我們好好享受山林，也為下一批遊客保持它的乾淨！

b.title: Why Mountains Matter More Than We Think
text: Mountains cover about a quarter of the world's land surface and are home to roughly 15 percent of its people. Yet their importance reaches far beyond the slopes. According to the United Nations, mountains supply fresh water to around half of humanity, which is why they are often called the water towers of the world. Rain and snow that fall on high ground feed rivers that flow to farms and cities far below.

To raise awareness of these benefits, the UN General Assembly declared December 11 International Mountain Day, which was first celebrated in 2003. Each year the day focuses on a different theme, from tourism to biodiversity. Schools, parks and mountain groups often hold walks and talks on the day.

Taiwan offers a striking example of mountain riches. Although the island is small, it has more than 200 peaks over 3,000 meters, and Yushan, at 3,952 meters, is the highest mountain in Northeast Asia. Within a few hours' drive, the landscape changes from tropical forest to alpine meadows. This helps explain the island's remarkable variety of plants and animals, many of which are found nowhere else on Earth.

Mountains, however, are under pressure. Climate change is warming many high places faster than the lowlands, shrinking glaciers and pushing cold-loving species uphill until they have nowhere left to go. Popular trails also face crowding, erosion and litter. In Taiwan, the authorities have encouraged hikers to follow the idea of leaving no trace and to bring all their trash back down with them.

Protecting mountains is not only a job for governments. Hikers can stay on marked trails, carry out what they bring in and respect local communities, including the Indigenous peoples who have lived in Taiwan's mountains for thousands of years. When we take care of the mountains, we are ultimately taking care of our own water, food and climate.
tz: 山地覆蓋了全球大約四分之一的陸地，住著大約 15% 的人口。然而，山的重要性遠遠超出山坡本身。根據聯合國的資料，山為大約一半的人類提供淡水，所以山常被稱為世界的「水塔」。落在高處的雨和雪匯成河流，流向遠在下游的農田和城市。
為了提高大眾對這些好處的認識，聯合國大會把 12 月 11 日訂為國際山岳日，2003 年第一次慶祝。每年這一天都有不同的主題，從觀光到生物多樣性都有。學校、公園和登山團體常在這天舉辦健行和講座。
台灣是山岳資源豐富的鮮明例子。雖然島嶼不大，卻有超過 200 座 3,000 公尺以上的高峰，而海拔 3,952 公尺的玉山是東北亞最高峰。開車幾個小時之內，地景就從熱帶森林變成高山草原。這也說明了台灣為什麼有驚人多樣的動植物，其中許多是地球上其他地方都找不到的。
然而，山正承受壓力。氣候變遷讓許多高地暖化得比低地更快，冰河縮小，喜歡寒冷的物種被迫往更高處移動，直到無處可去。熱門步道也面臨擁擠、侵蝕和垃圾問題。在台灣，主管機關鼓勵登山客實踐「無痕山林」的理念，把所有垃圾都帶下山。
保護山林不只是政府的工作。登山客可以走在標示清楚的步道上、把帶上山的東西帶下山，並尊重在地社區，包括在台灣山區生活了數千年的原住民族。當我們照顧山林時，最終照顧的是我們自己的水、食物和氣候。

c.title: Islands in the Sky: Mountains in a Warming World
text: Ecologists sometimes describe high mountains as sky islands. Just as a remote island isolates the species that live on it, a cold summit surrounded by warmer lowlands traps plants and animals that cannot survive below a certain height. Over thousands of years, such isolation produces unique species, and it also makes them unusually vulnerable.

Taiwan illustrates both sides. Rising steeply from the sea to nearly 4,000 meters, the island compresses climates that elsewhere are spread over thousands of kilometers. Its mountains shelter a high share of endemic species, such as the Formosan landlocked salmon, a fish left behind after the last ice age that survives only in a few cold streams in the Wuling area of central Taiwan, where it is strictly protected.

Climate change threatens this arrangement. Studies suggest that many mountain regions are warming faster than the global average, a pattern known as elevation-dependent warming, though the evidence varies by region. As temperatures rise, species shift upward to stay cool. But a mountain is roughly a cone: the higher one climbs, the less area remains, until there is no higher ground left. Biologists have a grim name for this process: the escalator to extinction.

People depend on these systems too. Mountain snow and glaciers act as natural reservoirs, releasing water during dry seasons to farms and cities far downstream. A 2020 study that ranked the world's mountain water towers found that the most important ones are also among the most threatened, because the populations relying on them are growing while their ice is shrinking.

How humans should use mountains is itself a matter of debate. In 2019, Taiwan's government announced a policy of opening up its mountains, simplifying permits and encouraging citizens to explore them. Supporters argued that people protect what they know and love; critics worried about more accidents, costly rescues and damage to fragile trails. Both concerns have merit, and the outcome depends largely on education and management rather than on access alone.

International Mountain Day, held each December 11, is a reminder that mountains are not simply scenery. They are water supplies, refuges for wildlife and cultural homelands. In a warming world, they may also be among the first places where the costs of inaction become impossible to ignore. Protecting them, in the end, means protecting ourselves as well.
tz: 生態學家有時把高山形容為「天空之島」。就像偏遠的島嶼會把島上的物種隔離起來，被較溫暖低地包圍的寒冷山頂，也困住了那些無法在某個高度以下生存的動植物。經過數千年，這樣的隔離孕育出獨特的物種，也讓牠們格外脆弱。
台灣正好說明了這兩面。台灣從海平面陡然升高到將近 4,000 公尺，把在其他地方分散在數千公里範圍內的氣候壓縮在一起。它的山區庇護了比例很高的特有種，例如櫻花鉤吻鮭——一種在上個冰河期之後被留下來的魚，如今只存活在台灣中部武陵地區少數幾條冰冷的溪流中，並受到嚴格保護。
氣候變遷威脅著這樣的格局。研究顯示，許多山區暖化的速度比全球平均更快，這種現象稱為「海拔依賴型暖化」，不過證據因地區而異。隨著氣溫上升，物種會往上移動以保持涼爽。但一座山大致是個圓錐體：越往上，剩下的面積越少，直到再也沒有更高的地方可去。生物學家為這個過程取了一個冷酷的名字：「通往滅絕的手扶梯」。
人類也依賴這些系統。山上的積雪和冰河就像天然水庫，在乾季時把水釋放給遠在下游的農田和城市。2020 年一項為全球山岳「水塔」排名的研究發現，最重要的水塔也正是受威脅最嚴重的，因為依賴它們的人口在增加，它們的冰卻在縮小。
人類應該如何使用山林，本身就是一個有爭議的問題。2019 年，台灣政府宣布「開放山林」政策，簡化入山申請，鼓勵民眾親近山林。支持者認為人會保護自己認識和喜愛的事物；批評者則擔心意外增加、搜救成本高昂，以及脆弱步道遭到破壞。兩方的顧慮都有道理，而結果主要取決於教育和管理，而不只是開放與否。
每年 12 月 11 日的國際山岳日提醒我們，山不只是風景。山是水源、是野生動物的避難所，也是文化的家園。在一個暖化的世界裡，山也可能是最早讓「不作為的代價」變得無法忽視的地方之一。說到底，保護山林，也就是保護我們自己。

topic: Word of the Year: Can One Word Sum Up a Year?
zh: 年度代表字：一個字能總結一整年嗎？
src: Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation · Oxford Languages · Merriam-Webster · United Daily News

a.title: One Word for a Whole Year
text: If you had to choose one word to describe this year, what would it be? Busy? Fun? Tired? Every December, people in many countries choose a word of the year.

In Japan, December 12 is Kanji Day. Around this day, a famous temple in Kyoto shows the kanji of the year. A monk writes the character with a big brush on a huge piece of paper. People all over Japan vote for the character, and the one with the most votes wins. In 2024, the kanji was 金, which means gold. Many people thought of Japan's gold medals at the Paris Olympics.

Taiwan has a word of the year too. People vote for one Chinese character. In 2023, the winner was 缺, which means not having enough. That year, people talked a lot about shortages of eggs, medicine and workers.
English dictionaries also choose words of the year. In 2023, Oxford chose rizz. It comes from the word charisma. Young people use it to talk about someone's charm.
Why do people like these words? A single word is easy to remember, and it helps us think about what happened. It can be happy, like gold, or worrying, like not having enough.
Try it yourself! Choose one word for your year and tell a friend why you chose it.
tz: 如果你得選一個字來形容今年，你會選什麼？忙？好玩？累？每年十二月，許多國家的人都會選出年度代表字。
在日本，12 月 12 日是「漢字日」。在這一天前後，京都一座有名的寺廟會公布年度漢字。一位僧侶用大毛筆把這個字寫在一張巨大的紙上。全日本的人投票選字，得票最多的字勝出。2024 年的漢字是「金」，意思是金子、金牌。很多人想到日本在巴黎奧運拿到的金牌。
台灣也有年度代表字。大家投票選出一個中文字。2023 年選出的是「缺」，意思是不夠、短缺。那一年大家常談到缺蛋、缺藥、缺工。
英文字典也會選年度代表字。2023 年，牛津選了 rizz。這個字來自 charisma（魅力）。年輕人用它來形容一個人很有魅力。
人們為什麼喜歡這些字？一個字很好記，也能幫助我們回想發生了什麼事。它可以是開心的，像「金」；也可以是令人擔心的，像「缺」。
自己試試看！為你的這一年選一個字，並告訴朋友你為什麼選它。

ph.exzh: 一想到夏天，我就想到芒果冰。

b.title: Can One Word Sum Up a Year?
text: Each December, dictionaries, newspapers and even temples announce a word of the year. In Japan, the kanji of the year is unveiled around December 12 at Kiyomizu-dera in Kyoto, where a senior monk paints the winning character with a giant brush. Taiwan has held a similar public vote for a Chinese character since 2008, and English dictionaries such as Oxford have named words of the year since the early 2000s.

Supporters say these lists work like a time capsule. A single word, they argue, captures the mood of a society more vividly than a long report. When Taiwanese voters chose 缺, meaning shortage, in 2023, the character summed up a year of empty egg shelves, missing medicines and companies struggling to find workers. Such choices also invite people to reflect together on what they have lived through. Looking back at past winners can also show how a country's worries change from one year to the next.

Critics are less impressed. Some point out that dictionary publishers use the announcements partly as marketing, selecting surprising slang to win headlines. Oxford's 2022 choice, goblin mode, was decided by a public online vote and puzzled many older readers. Others worry that reducing a complex year to one word oversimplifies events and leaves out people whose experiences were different.

In my view, both sides have a point, but the critics miss something. A word of the year is not meant to be a complete history; it is a conversation starter. Its real value lies less in the winning word than in the arguments it sparks about which events mattered, whose voices were heard and how language itself is changing.

So, rather than asking whether one word can sum up a year, perhaps we should ask a better question: what does the word we choose reveal about us? Our answer may say as much about us as about the year.
tz: 每年十二月，字典、報社甚至寺廟都會公布年度代表字。在日本，年度漢字在 12 月 12 日前後於京都清水寺揭曉，由一位資深僧侶用巨大的毛筆寫下獲選的字。台灣從 2008 年起也舉辦類似的公開投票，選出一個中文字；而像牛津這樣的英文字典，從 2000 年代初期就開始選出年度詞彙。
支持者說，這些名單就像時空膠囊。他們認為，一個字比一份長篇報告更能生動地捕捉社會的氛圍。2023 年台灣民眾選出意思是「短缺」的「缺」，這個字總結了蛋架空空、藥品缺貨、企業找不到人手的一整年。這樣的選擇也邀請大家一起回顧自己經歷過的事。回頭看看歷年的獲選字，也能看出一個國家的煩惱如何年年改變。
批評者則不以為然。有些人指出，字典出版商把公布年度字部分當成行銷手法，挑選令人意外的俚語來搶頭條。牛津 2022 年選出的 goblin mode（哥布林模式）是由網路公開投票決定的，讓許多年長讀者一頭霧水。另一些人擔心，把複雜的一年簡化成一個字會過度簡化事件，也忽略了經歷不同的人。
我認為雙方都有道理，但批評者忽略了一點。年度代表字本來就不是一部完整的歷史，而是一個開啟對話的話題。它真正的價值不在於獲選的字本身，而在於它引發的討論：哪些事件重要、誰的聲音被聽見，以及語言本身如何改變。
所以，與其問一個字能不能總結一整年，也許我們應該問一個更好的問題：我們選的字，透露了我們是什麼樣的人？我們的答案透露出的關於我們自己的事，可能跟關於這一年的一樣多。
gloss: 膠囊（time capsule 時空膠囊）

c.title: The Politics and Poetry of a Single Word
text: Every December, much of the world briefly agrees to play an unusual game: compressing twelve months of experience into a single word. The ritual takes different forms. In Japan, the Japan Kanji Aptitude Testing Foundation has organized a nationwide vote since 1995 and announces the result around December 12 at Kiyomizu-dera in Kyoto. The first winner, 震, meaning quake, reflected the devastating Kobe earthquake of that January.

English-language dictionaries take a more data-driven approach. Merriam-Webster bases its choice largely on which words people looked up most often, while Oxford combines evidence from huge collections of real-world text with the judgment of its lexicographers and, in some years, a public vote. The methods matter, because they determine whose language counts.

Defenders see the exercise as a valuable form of collective memory. Linguists note that new or newly popular words are sensitive indicators of social change: the spread of a term often reveals anxieties, technologies or values before they are fully discussed elsewhere. A word like 缺, meaning shortage, chosen by Taiwanese voters in 2023, preserves a shared sense of scarcity that statistics alone might not convey. In this sense, a list of past winners reads like a compressed diary of public life, recording what people laughed at, feared and argued about.

Skeptics raise sharper objections. Commercial dictionaries, they argue, have an obvious incentive to pick provocative slang that generates headlines and web traffic. Public votes can be dominated by organized online communities. And any single word inevitably privileges some experiences over others: a year remembered by one group as a triumph may be remembered by another as a time of loss.

Both perspectives contain truth. The word of the year is neither a scientific measurement nor a mere publicity stunt; it is a cultural performance that invites argument. Its usefulness depends on whether audiences treat it as a conclusion or as a prompt.

For language learners, the ritual offers a further lesson. Words are not fixed entries in a book but living tools, shaped by events and by the people who use them. Watching which words rise each year is one of the most direct ways to see a language, and a society, changing in real time. Learners who follow these lists also pick up new vocabulary that textbooks have not yet caught up with, and they gain a window into how people actually talk.
tz: 每年十二月，世界上很多地方都會短暫地一起玩一個不尋常的遊戲：把十二個月的經歷壓縮成一個字。這個儀式有不同的形式。在日本，日本漢字能力檢定協會從 1995 年起舉辦全國投票，並在 12 月 12 日前後於京都清水寺公布結果。第一個獲選的字是「震」，反映了那年一月造成重大傷亡的阪神大地震。
英語字典則採取更以數據為本的做法。韋氏字典主要根據大家最常查詢哪些字來決定；牛津則結合大量真實文本資料庫的證據、詞典編纂者的判斷，有些年份還加上公開投票。方法很重要，因為方法決定了誰的語言才算數。
支持者把這項活動視為一種寶貴的集體記憶。語言學家指出，新出現或突然流行的字是社會變化的敏感指標：一個詞的流行，往往在焦慮、科技或價值觀被其他地方充分討論之前，就先把它們透露出來。像台灣民眾在 2023 年選出、意思是「短缺」的「缺」，保存了一種共同的匱乏感，而這是單靠統計數字可能傳達不出來的。從這個角度看，歷年獲選字的清單就像一本濃縮的公共生活日記，記錄了人們笑過、怕過、爭論過的事。
懷疑者提出更尖銳的反對意見。他們認為，商業字典顯然有動機去挑選能製造頭條和網路流量的挑釁俚語。公開投票可能被有組織的網路社群主導。而且任何一個字都不可避免地偏重某些經歷：某個群體記得的勝利之年，在另一個群體記憶中可能是失落的一年。
兩種觀點都有道理。年度代表字既不是科學測量，也不只是宣傳噱頭；它是一場邀請大家辯論的文化表演。它有沒有用，取決於大眾把它當成結論，還是當成引發思考的起點。
對語言學習者來說，這個儀式還有另一個啟示。字詞不是書裡固定不變的條目，而是活的工具，被事件和使用它們的人所塑造。觀察每年哪些字崛起，是即時看見一種語言——以及一個社會——如何改變的最直接方法之一。追蹤這些清單的學習者，也能學到課本還來不及收錄的新詞彙，並一窺人們實際上怎麼說話。

topic: St. Lucia Day: Sweden's Festival of Light
zh: 聖露西亞節：瑞典的光明節
src: Sweden.se · Nordiska museet · Visit Sweden

a.title: A Crown of Candles
text: December in Sweden is very dark. In the north, the sun hardly comes up at all. But on the morning of December 13, a soft light appears in homes, schools and churches. It is St. Lucia Day.

Early in the morning, a girl in a long white dress walks slowly into the room. She has a red ribbon around her waist and a crown of candles on her head. She is Lucia. Other children follow her in a line. They hold candles and sing a beautiful, gentle song.
Many schools and towns choose a Lucia every year. Today, most crowns use electric candles, because real fire on someone's head can be dangerous.

Who was Lucia? The story says she was a young woman in Italy long ago. She brought food to poor people who were hiding in dark tunnels. She wore candles on her head so that her hands were free to carry the food.
On this day, Swedish families eat special yellow buns called lussekatter. They get their color from saffron, an expensive spice. People also eat thin ginger cookies and drink hot drinks together.
In the old calendar, December 13 was thought to be the longest night of the year. So Lucia Day is a festival of light in the darkest time. It reminds people that bright days will come back soon.
tz: 瑞典的十二月非常黑暗。在北部，太陽幾乎完全不會升起。但在 12 月 13 日早上，家裡、學校和教堂都會出現柔和的光。這一天是聖露西亞節。
一大早，一個穿著白色長裙的女孩慢慢走進房間。她腰上繫著紅緞帶，頭上戴著蠟燭做成的王冠。她就是「露西亞」。其他孩子排成一列跟在她後面，手拿蠟燭，唱著一首優美而溫柔的歌。
很多學校和城鎮每年都會選出一位露西亞。現在大多數王冠都改用電子蠟燭，因為頭上頂著真的火可能很危險。
露西亞是誰？傳說她是很久以前義大利的一位年輕女子。她把食物送給躲在黑暗地道裡的窮人。她把蠟燭戴在頭上，這樣雙手就能空出來拿食物。
在這一天，瑞典家庭會吃一種特別的黃色小麵包，叫做 lussekatter（露西亞貓麵包）。它們的顏色來自番紅花，一種昂貴的香料。大家也會一起吃薄薄的薑餅、喝熱飲。
在舊曆法中，12 月 13 日被認為是一年中最長的夜晚。所以露西亞節是在最黑暗的時節慶祝光明的節日，它提醒人們：明亮的日子很快就會回來。

b.title: Sankta Lucia: Light in the Darkest Season
text: In Stockholm in mid-December, the sun rises after 8:30 in the morning and sets before 3 p.m. Further north, above the Arctic Circle, it does not rise at all for weeks. Against this darkness, Swedes celebrate one of their best-loved traditions: Lucia Day on December 13.

The celebration centers on a procession. A girl chosen to play Lucia, dressed in white with a red sash and a crown of candles, leads a line of singers into a darkened room. Behind her come attendants holding candles and star boys wearing tall, pointed paper hats. Together they sing the traditional Lucia song, set to a melody that originally came from Naples in Italy. Schools, churches and workplaces hold their own processions, and the event is broadcast nationally on television.

The tradition combines several layers of history. Saint Lucy was a young Christian from Syracuse, Sicily, who was killed around the year 304. Her name is linked to the Latin word for light, and her feast day once fell on what the old Julian calendar treated as the longest night of the year. In Swedish folk belief, that night was dangerous, so families stayed up late, ate well and kept lights burning.

The modern form is surprisingly recent. In 1927, a Stockholm newspaper organized a public Lucia contest, and the white-robed procession spread across the country in the following decades. Today, many schools have dropped competitions altogether to avoid turning the celebration into a beauty contest, choosing Lucia by lottery instead.

With its saffron buns, ginger biscuits and candlelit songs, Lucia Day shows how a festival can borrow from religion, folk belief and the media, yet still feel ancient to those who celebrate it. For many Swedes, it marks the real start of the holiday season. Offices and cafés often serve coffee, buns and biscuits after their own small morning processions.
tz: 十二月中旬的斯德哥爾摩，太陽早上 8:30 之後才升起，下午 3 點前就落下。再往北，在北極圈以內，太陽好幾個星期完全不升起。在這樣的黑暗中，瑞典人慶祝他們最喜愛的傳統之一：12 月 13 日的露西亞節。
這個節慶的重心是一場遊行。被選來扮演露西亞的女孩身穿白衣、繫著紅色腰帶、頭戴蠟燭王冠，帶領一列歌者走進昏暗的房間。跟在她後面的是手持蠟燭的隨從，以及戴著高高尖頂紙帽的「星星男孩」。他們一起唱傳統的露西亞之歌，這首歌的旋律原本來自義大利的拿坡里。學校、教堂和職場都會舉辦自己的遊行，全國電視也會轉播這個活動。
這個傳統結合了好幾層歷史。聖露西亞是一位來自西西里島敘拉古的年輕基督徒，大約在西元 304 年遇害。她的名字和拉丁文的「光」有關，而她的節日曾經落在舊儒略曆認定為一年中最長的夜晚。在瑞典的民間信仰中，那一夜很危險，所以家家戶戶熬夜、吃得豐盛，並讓燈火整夜不熄。
現代的形式其實出奇地新。1927 年，斯德哥爾摩一家報社舉辦了公開的露西亞選拔，此後幾十年間，白袍遊行傳遍全國。如今，許多學校完全取消了選拔，以免把節慶變成選美比賽，改用抽籤選出露西亞。
有番紅花麵包、薑餅和燭光歌聲的露西亞節說明了：一個節日可以從宗教、民間信仰和媒體借用元素，卻仍讓慶祝的人覺得它古老悠久。對許多瑞典人來說，露西亞節才是節慶季節真正的開始。辦公室和咖啡館常在早上的小型遊行後，端出咖啡、麵包和餅乾。

c.title: Who Gets to Be Lucia? Tradition and Change
text: Each December 13, Swedes wake to the sound of the Lucia song and the glow of a crown of candles. For many, the ritual feels timeless, a link to ancestors who faced the same long winter nights. Historians, however, see it as a textbook example of what Eric Hobsbawm and Terence Ranger called an invented tradition: a practice that appears ancient but took its present shape relatively recently.

The ingredients are old. Saint Lucy, a martyr from fourth-century Sicily, gave the day its name, and her feast coincided, under the Julian calendar, with what was believed to be the longest night of the year. In rural Sweden, that night was associated with danger and supernatural beings, and people marked it with feasting and light. Yet the white-gowned figure leading a singing procession only spread widely in the twentieth century, helped along by a Stockholm newspaper's public Lucia contest in 1927 and later by radio and television.

Recognizing a tradition as invented does not make it fake. Invented traditions often fulfil real needs: they create a sense of continuity, bind communities together, give shape to the calendar and give children a role to play in public life. The Lucia procession does exactly that, uniting schools, churches and offices in a shared moment of warmth during the darkest weeks of the year.

But because traditions express who belongs, they also become sites of conflict. For decades, the chosen Lucia was typically a blonde girl, an image that some came to see as excluding Swedes of other backgrounds. Beauty-style contests have been criticized for judging girls on appearance, and many schools have replaced them with lotteries or allow any child who wishes to take part. When a department store advertisement in 2016 showed a boy dressed as Lucia, it set off a heated online debate.

Defenders of a more traditional Lucia argue that rituals lose meaning if their symbols can be changed at will. They worry that a festival which keeps changing to suit every trend may end up meaning very little to anyone. Others reply that the tradition has already changed many times, and that adapting it is how it survives.
The debate itself may be the best evidence of the festival's vitality. People rarely argue about traditions that no longer matter to them.
tz: 每年 12 月 13 日，瑞典人在露西亞之歌和蠟燭王冠的光芒中醒來。對許多人來說，這個儀式彷彿亙古不變，連結著曾經面對同樣漫長冬夜的祖先。然而，歷史學家把它看成艾瑞克・霍布斯邦和特倫斯・蘭杰所說的「被發明的傳統」的教科書範例：一種看起來古老、實際上卻是相對近期才成形的習俗。
它的成分很古老。來自四世紀西西里的殉道者聖露西亞為這一天命名，而在儒略曆下，她的節日恰好落在被認為一年中最長的夜晚。在瑞典鄉間，那一夜和危險及超自然生物聯想在一起，人們用宴飲和燈火來度過。然而，帶領歌唱遊行的白袍人物，是到了二十世紀才普及開來——1927 年斯德哥爾摩一家報社舉辦的公開露西亞選拔推了一把，之後的廣播和電視又進一步推廣。
承認一個傳統是「被發明的」，並不代表它是假的。被發明的傳統常常滿足真實的需求：它們創造延續感、凝聚社群，為一年的時序賦予形狀，也讓孩子在公共生活中有一個角色可以扮演。露西亞遊行正是如此，它讓學校、教堂和辦公室在一年中最黑暗的幾週裡，共享一段溫暖的時刻。
但因為傳統表達了「誰屬於這裡」，它們也會成為衝突的場域。幾十年來，獲選的露西亞通常是金髮女孩，有些人逐漸認為這種形象排除了其他背景的瑞典人。選美式的比賽被批評以外貌評判女孩，許多學校已改用抽籤，或讓任何想參加的孩子都能參加。2016 年，一家百貨公司的廣告呈現一個打扮成露西亞的男孩，引發了激烈的網路論戰。
主張維持較傳統露西亞形象的人認為，如果儀式的象徵可以隨意更改，儀式就會失去意義。他們擔心，一個為了迎合每股潮流而不斷改變的節日，最後可能對誰都沒什麼意義。另一些人則回應，這個傳統早已改變過許多次，而調整它正是它得以延續的方式。
這場爭論本身，也許正是這個節日充滿生命力的最佳證據。人們很少會為已經不在乎的傳統而爭吵。

a.title: Rights for Everyone
text: What do all people need? Food, a home, safety, school and the freedom to speak. These are called human rights. They belong to every person, everywhere, just because they are human. It doesn't matter where you live, what you look like or how much money you have.
On December 10, 1948, the United Nations agreed on a special paper called the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Universal means it is for everyone. That is why December 10 is Human Rights Day.
The declaration has 30 short articles. Article 1 says all people are born free and equal. Other articles say everyone has the right to go to school, to be safe and to have a fair trial.

The leader of the team that wrote it was Eleanor Roosevelt from the United States. People from many countries helped, including Chang Peng-chun from China. They wanted a world where the terrible things of World War II would never happen again.
The declaration is not a law, but it has been translated into more than 500 languages, and many countries used it to write their own laws.
Human rights are not only for big leaders. You can protect them in small ways every day, for example, by treating classmates fairly and speaking up when someone is bullied.
tz: 所有人都需要什麼？食物、住的地方、安全、上學，還有說話的自由。這些叫做人權。人權屬於每一個人、在每一個地方，只因為他們是人。不管你住在哪裡、長什麼樣子、有多少錢，都一樣。
1948 年 12 月 10 日，聯合國通過了一份特別的文件，叫做《世界人權宣言》。「世界的、普遍的」意思是它屬於每一個人。所以 12 月 10 日是世界人權日。
這份宣言有 30 條簡短的條文。第 1 條說所有人生而自由平等。其他條文說，每個人都有上學、得到安全保障和接受公平審判的權利。
帶領撰寫團隊的人是來自美國的愛蓮娜・羅斯福。許多國家的人也參與幫忙，包括來自中國的張彭春。他們希望世界上永遠不再發生第二次世界大戰那樣可怕的事。
這份宣言不是法律，但它已被翻譯成 500 多種語言，許多國家也用它來制定自己的法律。
人權不只是大人物的事。你每天都可以用小小的方式保護人權，例如公平對待同學，以及在有人被霸凌時挺身而出。

b.title: A Promise Made in 1948
text: On December 10, 1948, the United Nations General Assembly, meeting in Paris, adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights. Forty-eight countries voted in favor, none voted against, and eight abstained. Coming only three years after the end of World War II, the document was a response to the horrors of the war, including the Holocaust, and an attempt to set a common standard of achievement for all peoples and all nations.

The drafting committee was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt, the former First Lady of the United States, who was known for her patience and diplomatic skill. It also included the French lawyer René Cassin, the Lebanese philosopher Charles Malik and the Chinese scholar and diplomat Chang Peng-chun, who argued that the declaration should reflect not only Western ideas but also Confucian values such as concern for others.

The declaration's 30 articles cover civil and political rights, such as freedom of speech and a fair trial, as well as economic and social rights, such as the right to education and to work. It is not itself a binding treaty, but it inspired later agreements that are, including two international covenants adopted in 1966, and it has influenced constitutions around the world. It is also among the most translated documents ever, available in over 500 languages.

Taiwan offers an interesting case. Although it is not a UN member, in 2009 it passed a law making those two 1966 covenants part of its domestic legal system, and in 2020 it set up a National Human Rights Commission.

Nearly eight decades on, the promise remains unfinished. Rights are still violated in many places, and people continue to debate how to balance them. Yet the declaration's central idea, that dignity belongs to everyone and not only to citizens of powerful states, remains a standard against which governments can be judged.
tz: 1948 年 12 月 10 日，在巴黎開會的聯合國大會通過了《世界人權宣言》。48 個國家投下贊成票，沒有國家反對，8 國棄權。這份文件誕生於第二次世界大戰結束僅僅三年後，是對戰爭暴行（包括納粹大屠殺）的回應，也試圖為「所有人民和所有國家」訂下一個共同努力的標準。
起草委員會由美國前第一夫人愛蓮娜・羅斯福擔任主席，她以耐心和外交手腕著稱。成員還包括法國律師勒內・卡森、黎巴嫩哲學家查爾斯・馬利克，以及中國學者兼外交官張彭春。張彭春主張，宣言不應只反映西方思想，也要納入像「關懷他人」這樣的儒家價值。
宣言的 30 條條文涵蓋公民與政治權利，例如言論自由和公平審判，也涵蓋經濟與社會權利，例如受教育和工作的權利。宣言本身不是有約束力的條約，但它啟發了後來具約束力的協定，包括 1966 年通過的兩項國際公約，也影響了世界各地的憲法。它也是史上被翻譯最多的文件之一，有 500 多種語言版本。
台灣是個有趣的例子。雖然台灣不是聯合國會員，卻在 2009 年通過法律，讓那兩項 1966 年的公約成為國內法的一部分，並在 2020 年成立了國家人權委員會。
將近八十年後，這個承諾仍未完成。許多地方的人權仍遭侵害，人們也持續爭論該如何在各種權利之間取得平衡。然而，宣言的核心理念——尊嚴屬於每一個人，而不只屬於強國的公民——仍是評判各國政府的一把尺。

ph.ex: Most students voted in favor of a longer lunch break.
ph.exzh: 大多數學生投票贊成延長午休。

ph.m: not only Western ideas but also
ph.ex: She is not only smart but also kind.
ph.exzh: 她不但聰明，而且善良。

ph.ex: We need pens as well as paper.
ph.exzh: 我們需要筆，也需要紙。

ph.ex: Our school set up a new robotics club.
ph.exzh: 我們學校成立了新的機器人社。

ph.ex: The right to speak freely belongs to everyone.
ph.exzh: 自由說話的權利屬於每個人。

q.q: Which title best fits the passage?
opts: Eleanor Roosevelt's Busy Years Living in the White House in Washington
The Universal Declaration: Its Origins, Content and Lasting Influence
Why Taiwan Joined the United Nations as a Member in 2009
How World War II Was Finally Ended by a Vote in Paris
q.why: 第 1 段起源、第 2 段起草者、第 3 段內容、第 4–5 段影響。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: Several countries voted against the declaration in 1948.
The declaration only covers political rights such as free speech.
The declaration is a binding treaty that every court must enforce.
The people who drafted it came from different cultural backgrounds.
q.why: 第 2 段：起草者來自美、法、黎巴嫩、中國（換句話說）。沒有國家反對；也涵蓋經濟社會權利；它不是有約束力的條約。

q.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 4?
opts: To show how the declaration's ideas reached a place outside the UN
To describe the vote that took place in Paris in early December 1948
To explain why Chang Peng-chun valued Confucian ideas so much
To prove that human rights are never violated anywhere today
q.why: 第 4 段：台灣不是聯合國會員，卻把兩公約納入國內法並設立國家人權委員會。

q.q: The word “abstained” in paragraph 1 is closest in meaning to ___.
opts: voted strongly in favor of it
left the United Nations
chose not to vote either way
wrote a brand-new declaration
q.why: 第 1 段：贊成 48、反對 0，另外 8 國 abstained，就是「不投贊成也不投反對」＝棄權。

q.q: What can be inferred from the passage?
opts: Chang Peng-chun strongly opposed including any Western ideas in it at all.
Most human rights problems in the world ended soon after 1948.
The declaration's influence comes more from its ideas than from legal force.
The 1966 covenants completely replaced and cancelled the declaration.
q.why: 第 3 段：它 not itself a binding treaty，卻啟發條約和憲法；第 5 段它是評判政府的標準。

q.q: A post says: “The declaration isn't a law, so it doesn't matter.” Based on the passage, what is the best reply?
opts: It inspired binding treaties and laws, including some in Taiwan.
Right; no country has ever used it for anything important.
Right; it was cancelled when the 1966 covenants were adopted.
Wrong; it is a law that every citizen in the world must sign.
q.why: 第 3 段：inspired later agreements that are [binding]…influenced constitutions；第 4 段台灣把兩公約納入國內法。

tr.en: Forty-eight countries voted in favor, none voted against, and eight abstained.
tr.zh: 48 個國家投下贊成票，沒有國家反對，8 國棄權。

tr.en: It is also among the most translated documents ever, available in over 500 languages.
tr.zh: 它也是史上被翻譯最多的文件之一，有 500 多種語言版本。

tr.en: Rights are still violated in many places, and people continue to debate how to balance them.
tr.zh: 許多地方的人權仍遭侵害，人們也持續爭論該如何在各種權利之間取得平衡。

st.m: On December 10, 1948, the United Nations General Assembly, meeting in Paris, adopted the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.
st.mz: 1948 年聯合國通過《世界人權宣言》，它的核心理念「尊嚴屬於每一個人」至今仍然重要。
t: The drafting committee was chaired by Eleanor Roosevelt, the former First Lady of the United States, who was known for her patience and diplomatic skill.
The declaration's 30 articles cover civil and political rights, such as freedom of speech and a fair trial, as well as economic and social rights, such as the right to education and to work.
Taiwan offers an interesting case.
st.c: Yet the declaration's central idea, that dignity belongs to everyone and not only to citizens of powerful states, remains a standard against which governments can be judged.

c.title: Universal Rights in a Diverse World
text: When the Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted on December 10, 1948, its very first article made an ambitious claim: all human beings are born free and equal in dignity and rights. The word all has been both the declaration's greatest strength and the source of its most persistent controversy.

Critics have long questioned whether any list of rights can truly be universal. Even before the vote, the American Anthropological Association warned in 1947 that a statement reflecting the values of Western Europe and America might be imposed on cultures with different traditions. Decades later, in the 1993 Bangkok Declaration, several Asian governments argued that human rights must be understood in light of regional particularities, and suggested that development and stability could take priority over some individual freedoms. Some scholars still share this concern today.

Defenders respond that the declaration was never a purely Western product. Its drafters included the Chinese diplomat Chang Peng-chun, who drew on Confucian thought; the Lebanese philosopher Charles Malik; and the Indian delegate Hansa Mehta, who is credited with replacing the phrase all men with all human beings. Defenders also point out that the strongest objections to rights have often come from governments rather than from ordinary citizens, who rarely ask to be denied a fair trial or freedom from torture.

In the same year as the Bangkok Declaration, the World Conference on Human Rights in Vienna attempted a compromise. Its final document acknowledged that national and regional differences must be borne in mind, but insisted that states have a duty to protect all human rights regardless of their political, economic and cultural systems.

In practice, the debate has shifted from whether rights are universal to how they should be applied. A right to education, for example, can be fulfilled through very different school systems, and freedom of expression is limited in different ways by laws on defamation or hate speech. Universality, on this view, describes a shared floor of protections rather than a single, identical model of society that every country must copy.

Nearly eight decades on, that floor remains contested and unevenly respected. But the fact that governments now feel obliged to justify their conduct in the language of human rights, even when they violate them, suggests how deeply the declaration's ambition has taken root.
tz: 1948 年 12 月 10 日《世界人權宣言》通過時，它的第一條就提出了一個雄心勃勃的主張：人人生而自由，在尊嚴和權利上一律平等。「人人」這個詞，既是宣言最大的力量，也是它最持久爭議的來源。
批評者長期質疑，任何一份權利清單真的能普世適用嗎？甚至在表決之前，美國人類學會就在 1947 年警告，一份反映西歐和美國價值的聲明，可能會被強加在擁有不同傳統的文化上。數十年後，在 1993 年的《曼谷宣言》中，幾個亞洲國家政府主張，人權必須考量各地區的特殊性來理解，並暗示發展與穩定可以優先於某些個人自由。至今仍有一些學者抱持這樣的疑慮。
辯護者回應，這份宣言從來就不是純粹的西方產物。起草者包括援引儒家思想的中國外交官張彭春、黎巴嫩哲學家查爾斯・馬利克，以及被認為把「所有男人」改成「所有人類」的印度代表漢莎・梅塔。辯護者也指出，對人權最強烈的反對往往來自政府，而不是一般公民——很少有公民會要求被剝奪公平審判或免於酷刑的自由。
就在《曼谷宣言》發表的同一年，維也納世界人權會議試圖達成妥協。會議的最終文件承認，必須考慮各國與各地區的差異，但堅持各國不論其政治、經濟和文化制度為何，都有義務保護所有人權。
實際上，爭論的焦點已經從「人權是否普世」轉向「人權該如何落實」。例如，受教育的權利可以透過非常不同的學校制度來實現；言論自由也會以不同方式受到誹謗或仇恨言論相關法律的限制。依這個觀點，普世性描述的是一個共同的保障底線，而不是每個國家都必須照抄的單一、完全相同的社會模式。
將近八十年後，這條底線仍有爭議，各地遵守的程度也不一。但各國政府如今覺得必須用人權的語言為自己的作為辯護——即使是在侵害人權的時候——這個事實顯示，宣言的抱負已經多麼深地扎根。

ph.exzh: 考慮到颱風，校外教學取消了。

Defenders respond that the declaration was never a purely Western product.

topic: Rosa Parks: The Seat That Changed History
zh: 羅莎・帕克斯：一個座位改變歷史
src: Smithsonian · NPR · The Washington Post

a.title: She Said No
text: On December 1, 1955, a woman named Rosa Parks was riding a bus home from work in Montgomery, Alabama, in the United States.
At that time, the law said Black people had to give their bus seats to white people.
The bus driver told Rosa to stand up. She said no. The police came and took her to jail.
Black people in Montgomery were angry. For more than a year, they stopped riding the buses. They walked to work instead.
In 1956, the highest court in the country said the unfair bus law was wrong.
Rosa Parks showed that one brave person can help change the world.
tz: 1955 年 12 月 1 日，一位名叫羅莎・帕克斯的女士在美國阿拉巴馬州蒙哥馬利市，下班搭公車回家。
當時的法律規定，黑人必須把公車座位讓給白人。
公車司機叫羅莎站起來。她拒絕了。警察來了，把她帶進監獄。
蒙哥馬利的黑人非常憤怒。一年多的時間裡，他們不再搭公車，改成走路去上班。
1956 年，全國最高的法院宣布這條不公平的公車法律是錯的。
羅莎・帕克斯讓大家看到：一個勇敢的人，就能幫忙改變世界。

ph.ex: Please stand up when the teacher comes in.
ph.exzh: 老師進來時請起立。

ph.ex: I was only six at that time.
ph.exzh: 那時我才六歲。

ph.ex: It was raining, so we played inside instead.
ph.exzh: 下雨了，所以我們改在室內玩。

ph.ex: More than thirty students joined the club.
ph.exzh: 超過三十個學生加入了社團。

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How Rosa Parks's brave choice helped end an unfair bus law
How buses in Montgomery were driven in 1955
Why people in Alabama liked to walk to work every day after work
How the police in Alabama worked every day
q.why: 全文介紹帕克斯的勇敢行動如何終結不公平法律。

q.q: According to the reading, which is TRUE?
opts: Rosa Parks gave her seat to a white passenger when she was asked.
The highest court said the bus law was fair in 1956.
Rosa was riding a bus to work in the morning.
Black people in Montgomery stopped riding buses for over a year.
q.why: 第 4 段：For more than a year, they stopped riding the buses。她拒絕讓座；最高法院說這條法律是錯的；她是下班搭車「回家」。

q.q: Which is the right order? (a) The court said the bus law was wrong. (b) Rosa refused to stand up. (c) People stopped riding the buses.
q.why: 羅莎拒絕起身（第 3 段）→ 黑人一年多不搭公車（第 4 段）→ 1956 年法院判決（第 5 段）。

q.q: In the text, “unfair” means ___.
opts: very old and slow
not right or equal for everyone
easy to follow
very old, slow and boring for most people
q.why: unfair = 不公平的。

q.q: Why did people walk to work instead of taking the bus?
opts: Because the buses were broken
Because walking was faster
To protest against the unfair law
Because the police told them to
q.why: 第四段：他們很生氣，拒搭公車表達抗議。

q.q: Your school has a rule that you think is unfair to some students. Based on Rosa Parks's story, what is a good first step?
opts: Break things at school so everyone can see you are angry
Say nothing, because rules can never change
Make fun of the students the rule helps
Speak up calmly and work with others to change it
q.why: 故事啟示：勇敢、和平地發聲，並和他人一起努力。

b.title: More Than Tired Feet
text: On December 1, 1955, Rosa Parks, a 42-year-old seamstress, refused to give up her bus seat to a white passenger in Montgomery, Alabama. Under the city's segregation laws, she was arrested.

Her arrest sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott. For 381 days, tens of thousands of Black residents refused to ride city buses, walking or sharing cars instead. A young minister named Martin Luther King Jr. became the boycott's leader and rose to national fame.
In 1956, the US Supreme Court ruled that segregation on public buses was unconstitutional, and the boycott ended in victory.

Parks is often remembered as a tired seamstress who simply wanted to sit down. In fact, she was an experienced activist who worked for the civil rights group NAACP and had trained in nonviolent protest. As she later explained, she was not tired physically; she was tired of giving in.
Others had resisted before her, including 15-year-old Claudette Colvin earlier that year. Their courage reminds us that movements are built by many people.
tz: 1955 年 12 月 1 日，42 歲的裁縫羅莎・帕克斯在阿拉巴馬州蒙哥馬利，拒絕把公車座位讓給一名白人乘客。依照該市的種族隔離法，她被逮捕了。
她的被捕引發了蒙哥馬利公車抵制運動。在 381 天裡，數萬名黑人居民拒搭市公車，改成走路或共乘。一位名叫馬丁・路德・金恩的年輕牧師成為抵制運動的領袖，也因此全國知名。
1956 年，美國最高法院裁定公車上的種族隔離違憲，抵制運動以勝利告終。
帕克斯常被記成一個只是想坐下休息的疲累裁縫。事實上，她是一位經驗豐富的運動人士，為民權團體 NAACP 工作，也受過非暴力抗爭的訓練。她後來解釋，她不是身體累，而是厭倦了一再屈服。
在她之前也有人反抗過，包括同年稍早 15 歲的克勞黛特・柯爾文。她們的勇氣提醒我們：社會運動是由許多人一起建立的。

ph.ex: Don't give up your seat if you are feeling sick yourself.
ph.exzh: 如果你自己也不舒服，就不用讓座。

ph.ex: In fact, the test was easier than I thought.
ph.exzh: 事實上，考試比我想的簡單。

ph.ex: I'm tired of eating instant noodles every night.
ph.exzh: 我厭倦每晚吃泡麵了。

ph.ex: My parents finally gave in and let me get a puppy.
ph.exzh: 我爸媽終於讓步，讓我養小狗。

ph.ex: The singer rose to fame after one video went viral.
ph.exzh: 那位歌手因一支影片爆紅而成名。

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Rosa Parks was a tired seamstress who sat down by accident and had never taken part in any kind of protest before.
Rosa Parks, an experienced activist, sparked a boycott that helped end bus segregation, as part of a wider movement.
Martin Luther King Jr. was arrested on a bus in Montgomery in 1955 and started a boycott alone.
Claudette Colvin led the Montgomery Bus Boycott for 381 days and then joined the Supreme Court.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：經驗豐富的運動者、抵制運動、更廣大的社會運動。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: Parks had trained in nonviolent protest before her arrest.
The Montgomery Bus Boycott lasted for only 181 days in total.
Martin Luther King Jr. was already famous before the boycott.
Claudette Colvin resisted a few years after Rosa Parks.
q.why: 第 4 段：she was an experienced activist who … had trained in nonviolent protest。抵制持續 381 天；金恩是在抵制中才成名；柯爾文是「同一年稍早」。

q.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 4?
opts: To describe what happened on the bus that day
To explain the Supreme Court's 1956 decision
To show that Parks was too tired to stand
To correct a common but simple image of Parks
q.why: 第 4 段：常被記成「累了想坐下的裁縫」，In fact 她是有經驗的運動人士——在修正一般人的印象。

q.q: In paragraph 2, a “boycott” is ___.
opts: a type of public city bus
a court decision about laws on public buses
refusing to use or buy something as a protest
a kind of church meeting
q.why: boycott = 抵制。

q.q: What did Parks mean by being “tired of giving in”?
opts: Her feet hurt after a long day at work
She was tired of accepting unfair treatment
She wanted to stop being a seamstress
She was tired of riding the buses every day
q.why: 第四段：不是身體累，而是厭倦屈服於不公。

q.q: A short video says: “Rosa Parks just had tired feet and changed history by accident.” Based on the text, how accurate is this?
opts: Accurate: she simply wanted to sit down after work
Accurate: she had never even heard of civil rights groups
Not accurate: she actually drove the bus that day
Not accurate: she was a trained activist and chose to resist
q.why: 第四段：她是受過訓練的運動人士。

tr.en: Under the city's segregation laws, she was arrested.
tr.zh: 依照該市的種族隔離法，她被逮捕了。

tr.en: As she later explained, she was not tired physically; she was tired of giving in.
tr.zh: 她後來解釋，她不是身體累，而是厭倦了一再屈服。

tr.en: Their courage reminds us that movements are built by many people.
tr.zh: 她們的勇氣提醒我們，社會運動是由許多人一起建立的。

st.m: Their courage reminds us that movements are built by many people.
st.mz: 帕克斯是經驗豐富的運動者，她的拒絕引發了公車抵制運動；社會運動是由許多人一起完成的。
t: Her arrest sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott.
In 1956, the US Supreme Court ruled that segregation on public buses was unconstitutional, and the boycott ended in victory.
Parks is often remembered as a tired seamstress who simply wanted to sit down.
st.c: Their courage reminds us that movements are built by many people.

c.title: The Myth of the Tired Seamstress
text: History likes its heroes simple. The popular image of Rosa Parks, a weary seamstress who on December 1, 1955, was simply too tired to give her seat to a white man, is moving, memorable and misleading.

Parks was in fact a seasoned organiser. She had served for years as secretary of the Montgomery branch of the NAACP, investigated cases of racial violence, and attended training in nonviolent resistance. Her refusal was not an impulse but a considered act by someone who understood exactly what arrest would mean.

Local activists had been waiting for a case strong enough to challenge segregation. Earlier in 1955, fifteen-year-old Claudette Colvin had been arrested for the same act, but organisers judged that Parks, respected and composed, could rally wider support.

The result was the Montgomery Bus Boycott, a 381-day campaign of extraordinary discipline that launched Martin Luther King Jr. to prominence and ended when the Supreme Court declared bus segregation unconstitutional.

Remembering Parks accurately does not diminish her courage; it enlarges it. Change came not from a single tired moment but from preparation, strategy and the collective sacrifice of thousands who walked.
tz: 歷史喜歡簡單的英雄。大眾印象中的羅莎・帕克斯——一位疲憊的裁縫，在 1955 年 12 月 1 日只是累到不想把座位讓給白人男子——令人感動、好記，卻也容易誤導。
事實上，帕克斯是一位資深的組織者。她多年擔任 NAACP 蒙哥馬利分會的秘書，調查種族暴力案件，也參加過非暴力抗爭的訓練。她的拒絕不是一時衝動，而是一個完全明白被捕意味著什麼的人，經過深思熟慮的行動。
當地運動人士一直在等待一個足以挑戰種族隔離的有力案例。1955 年稍早，15 歲的克勞黛特・柯爾文也曾因同樣的舉動被捕，但組織者判斷，受人敬重又沉著冷靜的帕克斯，更能凝聚廣泛的支持。
結果就是蒙哥馬利公車抵制運動——一場長達 381 天、紀律非凡的行動，讓馬丁・路德・金恩躍上全國舞台，並在最高法院宣布公車種族隔離違憲時畫下句點。
準確地記得帕克斯，並不會減損她的勇氣，反而會放大它。改變並非來自單一疲累的瞬間，而是來自準備、策略，以及數千名徒步者共同的犧牲。

ph.ex: He looks shy, but in fact he loves to talk.
ph.exzh: 他看起來害羞，但事實上很愛聊天。

ph.ex: Success comes not from luck but from practice.
ph.exzh: 成功不是來自運氣，而是來自練習。

ph.ex: We are waiting for the bus in the rain.
ph.exzh: 我們正在雨中等公車。

ph.ex: The class president tried to rally support for a beach clean-up.
ph.exzh: 班長努力凝聚大家對淨灘活動的支持。

ph.ex: My best friend and I have the same birthday.
ph.exzh: 我和最好的朋友同一天生日。

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Rosa Parks acted on a sudden impulse because she was tired after a long day at work.
The simple 'tired seamstress' story hides the planning and collective effort behind Parks's courageous act.
Claudette Colvin, not Rosa Parks, deserves all the credit for ending bus segregation in Montgomery and the whole boycott.
The boycott failed, and bus segregation continued in Montgomery for many years.
q.why: 主旨：簡化的故事掩蓋了背後的準備與集體努力。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “seasoned” means ___.
opts: experienced from much practice
tired from hard work
young and very new to the job
angry and impatient
q.why: seasoned = 經驗豐富的。

q.q: Why did organisers choose Parks's case rather than Colvin's?
opts: Colvin's arrest happened in a different city, so it could not be used
Colvin had not actually refused her seat
Parks asked them to forget about Colvin
They judged Parks, respected and composed, could rally wider support
q.why: 第三段：organisers judged that Parks … could rally wider support。

q.q: How does the writer describe the popular image of Parks?
opts: As completely false and harmful
As accurate in every detail
As moving but misleading
As boring and unimportant
q.why: 第一段：moving, memorable and misleading。

q.q: What does the final paragraph argue?
opts: The boycott was a mistake
Only King should be remembered
History should keep heroes simple so that children can remember them
Accurate memory enlarges rather than diminishes her courage
q.why: 最後一段：does not diminish her courage; it enlarges it。

q.q: A textbook summary reads: “One tired woman changed America in a single moment.” What would make it more accurate?
opts: Adding her years of activism and the thousands who joined the boycott
Removing her name and the date from the summary
Saying the Supreme Court changed the law before her arrest in 1955
Saying the boycott lasted only one afternoon
q.why: 第二、五段：準備、策略與集體犧牲。

st.m: Remembering Parks accurately does not diminish her courage; it enlarges it.
st.mz: 正確地記住帕克斯不會減損她的勇氣，反而更凸顯它：改變來自準備、策略和許多人的共同犧牲。
t: Parks was in fact a seasoned organiser.
Local activists had been waiting for a case strong enough to challenge segregation.

The result was the Montgomery Bus Boycott, a 381-day campaign of extraordinary discipline that launched Martin Luther King Jr. to prominence and ended when the Supreme Court declared bus segregation unconstitutional.
st.c: Change came not from a single tired moment but from preparation, strategy and the collective sacrifice of thousands who walked.

Why do you think people like to remember heroes as simple, lucky people?

topic: The Great Barrier Reef
zh: 大堡礁：海底的彩色城市
src: UNESCO · Nature · The Guardian

a.title: A Rainbow Under the Sea
text: The Great Barrier Reef is in the sea near Australia. It is the biggest coral reef in the world.
It is more than 2,000 kilometres long. Thousands of colourful fish, turtles and sharks live there.
Coral looks like a rock or a plant, but it is really a group of tiny animals.
Many visitors go snorkelling there to see the beautiful colours under the water.
But the reef is in danger. When the sea gets too hot, the coral turns white. This is called bleaching. If the water stays hot, the coral can die.
People are working hard to protect the reef for the future.
tz: 大堡礁位在澳洲附近的海裡，是世界上最大的珊瑚礁。
它長達兩千多公里，有成千上萬種五顏六色的魚、海龜和鯊魚住在那裡。
珊瑚看起來像石頭或植物，但其實是一群很小的動物。
很多遊客會去那裡浮潛，欣賞水下美麗的色彩。
但是珊瑚礁正面臨危險。海水太熱時，珊瑚會變白，這叫做白化。如果海水一直很熱，珊瑚就可能死掉。
人們正努力保護珊瑚礁，讓它留給未來。

ph.ex: That cloud looks like a rabbit!
ph.exzh: 那朵雲看起來像一隻兔子！

ph.ex: She is working hard for the English contest.
ph.exzh: 她正為英文比賽努力準備。

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to go snorkelling safely in the sea near Australia
Why sharks are dangerous to visitors
The Great Barrier Reef, its life and its dangers
How coral turns into rocks and plants
q.why: 全文介紹大堡礁、生物與危機。

The reef is about 200 kilometres long.

q.q: In paragraph 5, what does "This" in "This is called bleaching" refer to?

coral turning white
visitors snorkelling
fish leaving the reef

visitors swimming and diving under the water
coral growing bigger every year
coral turning white when the sea is too hot
q.why: 第五段：the coral turns white. This is called bleaching。

q.q: Why is hot water a problem for the reef?

It brings too many visitors

q.q: Your family is going snorkelling on a reef. Based on the text, which action helps protect it?
opts: Take a piece of coral home as a gift
Look at the coral but never touch or stand on it
Feed the fish with your bread
Take a small piece of coral home as a gift for your family

gt.en: It is the biggest coral reef in the world.
gt.zh: 它是世界上最大的珊瑚礁。

gt.en: Coral looks like a rock or a plant, but it is really a group of tiny animals.

b.title: A Living Wonder Under Pressure
text: Stretching for more than 2,300 kilometres off the coast of Queensland, Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system on Earth. It is made up of about 2,900 individual reefs and hundreds of islands.
Corals are tiny animals that live together in colonies. Many of them depend on microscopic algae living inside their bodies, which provide food and give the reef its brilliant colours.
The reef was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981, and it attracts millions of visitors who come to dive, snorkel and sail.

However, rising sea temperatures have caused repeated mass bleaching events in recent years. When water stays too warm, corals push out their algae and turn white. Bleached corals can recover if temperatures fall, but long heatwaves can kill them.
Pollution running off farms and outbreaks of coral-eating starfish add to the stress. Scientists say cutting greenhouse gas emissions is the most important way to give the reef a future.
tz: 大堡礁沿著澳洲昆士蘭外海綿延兩千三百多公里，是地球上最大的珊瑚礁系統，由大約兩千九百座獨立礁體和數百座島嶼組成。
珊瑚是群居生活的微小動物。許多珊瑚依賴住在體內的微小藻類，藻類提供養分，也讓珊瑚礁呈現燦爛的色彩。
大堡礁在 1981 年被列為聯合國教科文組織世界遺產，每年吸引數百萬名遊客前來潛水、浮潛和航行。
然而，近年海水溫度上升，造成一次又一次大規模白化。海水持續太暖時，珊瑚會把藻類排出、變成白色。如果水溫下降，白化的珊瑚有機會恢復，但長時間的海洋熱浪可能讓它們死亡。
農田流出的汙染，以及吃珊瑚的海星大量爆發，也增加了壓力。科學家表示，減少溫室氣體排放，是讓大堡礁擁有未來最重要的方法。

ph.ex: Our class is made up of twenty-eight students.
ph.exzh: 我們班由二十八位學生組成。

ph.ex: Many students depend on their phones to check the time.
ph.exzh: 很多學生依賴手機看時間。

ph.ex: In recent years, more people have started riding bikes to school.
ph.exzh: 近年來，更多人開始騎腳踏車上學。

ph.ex: The noise added to my stress before the exam.
ph.exzh: 噪音加重了我考前的壓力。

ph.ex: I wanted to go out. However, it started to rain.
ph.exzh: 我想出門，然而開始下雨了。

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The Great Barrier Reef was named a World Heritage Site in 1981 because so many people visit it.
Coral-eating starfish are the only reason the Great Barrier Reef is in serious danger.
The Great Barrier Reef is a huge living wonder, but warming seas and other stresses threaten it.
Bleached corals always recover quickly, so the reef will not change in the future.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：巨大的生命奇觀，卻受暖化與其他壓力威脅。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: The reef was named a World Heritage Site back in 1891.
Bleached corals may recover if the water cools down.
Corals push out their algae when the water is too cold.
Starfish are the most important cause of bleaching.
q.why: 第 4 段：Bleached corals can recover if temperatures fall。1981 年列入世界遺產；是水「太暖」時排出藻類；造成白化的是海水升溫，海星只是額外的壓力。

q.q: Which best describes how the passage is organised?
opts: Facts about the reef, then threats, then a possible solution
A story of one diver's trip, followed by advice for tourists
A list of fish species, then where to see them
Arguments for and against visiting the reef
q.why: 第 1–3 段介紹大堡礁，第 4–5 段說明白化、污染等威脅，最後提出減碳是最重要的解方。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “recover” means ___.
opts: turn completely white
move to a new place
grow much bigger
get healthy again
q.why: recover = 恢復。

q.q: Why do bleached corals look white?
opts: They have pushed out the coloured algae
They are covered by sand
They are painted white by visitors every summer
They have grown new shells
q.why: 第二、四段：顏色來自藻類，排出藻類就變白。

q.q: A tourist ad says: “The reef is fine — just visit and enjoy!” Based on the text, what is missing?
opts: That the reef is longer than 3,000 kilometres in total from end to end
That rising sea temperatures have caused repeated bleaching
That snorkelling is not allowed
That the reef has no animals
q.why: 第四段：近年反覆發生大規模白化。

tr.en: Corals are tiny animals that live together in colonies.
tr.zh: 珊瑚是群居生活的微小動物。

tr.en: Bleached corals can recover if temperatures fall, but long heatwaves can kill them.
tr.zh: 如果水溫下降，白化的珊瑚有機會恢復，但長時間的熱浪可能讓它們死亡。

tr.en: Pollution running off farms and outbreaks of coral-eating starfish add to the stress.
tr.zh: 農田流出的汙染和吃珊瑚的海星大量爆發，也增加了壓力。

st.m: Stretching for more than 2,300 kilometres off the coast of Queensland, Australia, the Great Barrier Reef is the largest coral reef system on Earth.
st.mz: 大堡礁是世界最大的珊瑚礁系統，正受到海水暖化和污染的威脅；減少溫室氣體是最重要的保護方法。
t: Corals are tiny animals that live together in colonies.
The reef was named a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1981, and it attracts millions of visitors who come to dive, snorkel and sail.
However, rising sea temperatures have caused repeated mass bleaching events in recent years.
st.c: Scientists say cutting greenhouse gas emissions is the most important way to give the reef a future.

c.title: The Reef That Measures the Planet
text: Seen from above, the Great Barrier Reef looks like a scattering of turquoise jewels along Australia's northeast coast. In reality it is a vast partnership: billions of coral polyps living in symbiosis with microscopic algae that feed them sunlight's energy and paint them in brilliant colour.

That partnership is precise and fragile. When the surrounding water stays even a degree or two above normal for weeks, the stressed corals expel their algae and turn ghostly white. Bleaching is not immediately fatal, but prolonged heat starves corals to death.

Since 2016 the reef has endured a series of mass bleaching events, an unprecedented frequency that leaves corals little time to recover between heatwaves. Agricultural runoff and outbreaks of crown-of-thorns starfish compound the damage.

Local measures, including improving water quality, culling starfish and breeding heat-tolerant corals, can buy time. Yet scientists stress that none can substitute for reducing the greenhouse gas emissions that are warming the oceans.
In that sense the reef has become a kind of planetary instrument, its colours recording, year by year, decisions made far from its waters.
tz: 從空中俯瞰，大堡礁像一串散落在澳洲東北海岸的綠松石珠寶。實際上，它是一場龐大的合作：數十億隻珊瑚蟲與微小藻類共生，藻類把陽光的能量提供給珊瑚當養分，也替它們染上燦爛的色彩。
這種合作既精確又脆弱。周圍海水只要連續幾週比平常高出一、兩度，受壓力的珊瑚就會把藻類排出，變成慘白色。白化不會立刻致命，但長時間的高溫會讓珊瑚活活餓死。
自 2016 年以來，大堡礁經歷了一連串大規模白化，頻率前所未見，讓珊瑚在兩次熱浪之間幾乎沒有時間恢復。農業逕流和棘冠海星的大量爆發，更讓損害雪上加霜。
在地的措施——改善水質、撲殺海星、培育耐熱珊瑚——可以爭取時間。然而科學家強調，這些都無法取代減少讓海洋變暖的溫室氣體排放。
從這個意義上說，大堡礁已經成為一種觀測地球的儀器：它的色彩年復一年記錄著，在遠離這片海域的地方所做的決定。

ph.ex: The test looked hard, but in reality it was quite easy.
ph.exzh: 考試看起來很難，實際上相當簡單。

ph.ex: He asked a question to buy time before answering.
ph.exzh: 他先問了一個問題，爭取回答前的時間。

ph.ex: Videos can't substitute for real practice.
ph.exzh: 影片無法取代實際練習。

ph.ex: Mistakes help us learn. In that sense, they are useful.
ph.exzh: 錯誤能幫助我們學習。從那個意義上說，錯誤是有用的。

ph.ex: Year by year, my handwriting is getting better.
ph.exzh: 一年又一年，我的字越寫越好。

ph.ex: Even a degree or two can change how plants grow.
ph.exzh: 即使只差一兩度，也會影響植物生長。

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: The reef is mainly threatened by tourists, so closing it to all visitors would fully solve the problem of bleaching.
Breeding heat-tolerant corals has already solved the problem of bleaching on the reef.
Bleaching is always fatal, so there is no longer any hope for the Great Barrier Reef.
The reef's fragile partnership is being broken by ocean warming, so its fate depends mostly on global emission cuts.
q.why: 主旨：脆弱的共生被暖化破壞，命運取決於全球減排。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “unprecedented” means ___.
opts: happening once a year
never having happened before
slowly getting smaller each year
easy to predict
q.why: unprecedented = 前所未有的。

q.q: Why is the frequency of bleaching events so dangerous?
opts: Corals get little time to recover between heatwaves
Visitors can no longer see the bright colours of the reef
Starfish stop eating coral
Algae become too colourful
q.why: 第三段：little time to recover between heatwaves。

q.q: How does the writer view local measures like culling starfish?
opts: Completely useless and harmful, so they should be stopped right away
The only real solution needed
Useful for buying time but not a substitute for cutting emissions
Too expensive to try
q.why: 第四段：can buy time. Yet … none can substitute。

q.q: What image does the final paragraph use?
opts: The reef as an instrument recording distant decisions
The reef as a row of jewels
The reef as a busy city under the sea, full of traffic
The reef as a rainbow
q.why: 結尾：a kind of planetary instrument。

q.q: A government spends money only on breeding heat-tolerant corals and ignores emissions. Based on the essay, what is the best criticism?
opts: It is the perfect plan, because heat-tolerant corals will solve everything
It may buy time, but cannot replace cutting the emissions warming the oceans

q.why: 第四段的論點。

st.m: In reality it is a vast partnership: billions of coral polyps living in symbiosis with microscopic algae that feed them sunlight's energy and paint them in brilliant colour.
st.mz: 大堡礁是珊瑚與藻類之間脆弱的共生關係，它的變化記錄著人類在遠方做出的決定。
t: That partnership is precise and fragile.
Since 2016 the reef has endured a series of mass bleaching events, an unprecedented frequency that leaves corals little time to recover between heatwaves.
Local measures, including improving water quality, culling starfish and breeding heat-tolerant corals, can buy time.
st.c: In that sense the reef has become a kind of planetary instrument, its colours recording, year by year, decisions made far from its waters.

topic: 'Merry Christmas': The First Text Message
zh: 「聖誕快樂」：世界第一則手機簡訊
src: BBC · TIME · Taipei Times

a.title: Two Words That Started It All
text: On December 3, 1992, a young engineer in Britain named Neil Papworth sent a short message to a phone.
The message said just two words: 'Merry Christmas'. It was the first text message in the world!
Neil sent it from a computer, because phones at that time had no keyboards for typing.
The phone belonged to his boss. His boss was at a Christmas party, and he could not reply.

b.title: From 160 Characters to Billions of Chats
text: On December 3, 1992, Neil Papworth, a 22-year-old engineer working for a company in Britain, typed 'Merry Christmas' on a computer and sent it to the mobile phone of a Vodafone director, Richard Jarvis. It was the first SMS, or text message, ever sent.
Jarvis was at an office Christmas party and could not answer, partly because phones at the time could not send texts, only receive them.
Text messaging grew slowly at first but exploded once phones could send messages and networks allowed texts between different companies.

Each message was limited to 160 characters. That limit is often credited to the German engineer Friedhelm Hillebrand, who reportedly found that most postcards and short notes could fit within it. To save space, users invented abbreviations such as 'gr8' and 'c u l8r'.
Today, apps like LINE carry billions of messages with photos, voice notes and stickers. In 2021, that first message was even sold as a digital collectible for more than 100,000 euros.
tz: 1992 年 12 月 3 日，在英國一家公司工作的 22 歲工程師尼爾・帕普沃斯，在電腦上打了「Merry Christmas」，傳到沃達豐公司主管理查・賈維斯的手機上。這是史上第一則 SMS，也就是手機簡訊。
賈維斯當時正在參加公司的聖誕派對，沒辦法回覆，部分原因是那時的手機只能接收簡訊，不能傳送。
簡訊一開始成長緩慢，但等到手機可以傳訊、不同電信公司之間也能互傳後，就爆炸性地普及。
每則簡訊限制 160 個字元。這個上限常被歸功於德國工程師弗里德赫姆・希勒布蘭德，據說他發現大多數明信片和短箋都能塞進這個長度。為了省空間，使用者發明了像「gr8」和「c u l8r」這樣的縮寫。
如今，LINE 等應用程式每天傳遞數十億則訊息，附帶照片、語音和貼圖。2021 年，那第一則簡訊甚至以數位收藏品的形式，賣出十萬多歐元。

c.title: A Greeting Nobody Answered
text: The first text message was, fittingly, a greeting that went unanswered. On December 3, 1992, engineer Neil Papworth typed 'Merry Christmas' into a computer and sent it to a Vodafone executive's handset, which, like most phones of the era, could receive such messages but not reply.

Few at the time imagined that the Short Message Service would matter much. It had been designed partly as a technical afterthought, a way to use spare capacity in the network's signalling channels, and its 160-character ceiling reflected engineering constraints as much as any theory of human communication.

Constraint, however, bred creativity. Users compressed language into abbreviations, numerals and emoticons, a playful shorthand that critics feared would corrode spelling and that linguists later argued was simply a new register people switched in and out of.

Within two decades, texting had reshaped social life: friendships, protests and even breakups were conducted in brief bursts of text. Messaging apps have since absorbed the habit, adding images, voice notes and read receipts.
The original 'Merry Christmas', auctioned as a digital collectible in 2021, is now less a message than a monument, a reminder that revolutions can begin as modest experiments.
tz: 第一則手機簡訊，很應景地，是一句沒有人回覆的問候。1992 年 12 月 3 日，工程師尼爾・帕普沃斯在電腦上打了「Merry Christmas」，傳到沃達豐一位主管的手機上——那支手機和當時大多數手機一樣，能接收這種訊息，卻不能回覆。
當時很少人想到簡訊服務會有多重要。它某種程度上只是技術上的附帶設計，用來利用網路信令頻道中多餘的容量；而 160 個字元的上限，與其說反映了某種人類溝通的理論，不如說同樣反映了工程上的限制。
然而，限制催生了創意。使用者把語言壓縮成縮寫、數字和表情符號；批評者擔心這種俏皮的速記會侵蝕拼字能力，語言學家後來則主張，這只是人們可以自由切換進出的一種新語體。
不到二十年，簡訊就重塑了社交生活：友誼、抗議，甚至分手，都在一段段簡短的文字中進行。後來的通訊軟體吸收了這個習慣，再加上圖片、語音訊息和已讀標記。
那則原始的「Merry Christmas」在 2021 年以數位收藏品形式拍賣，如今與其說是一則訊息，不如說是一座紀念碑——提醒我們，革命也可以從一個不起眼的實驗開始。

ph.exzh: 睡眠和讀書一樣重要。

ph.ex: For me, the trip was less a holiday than a lesson.
ph.exzh: 對我來說，那趟旅行與其說是度假，不如說是一堂課。

ph.exzh: 二十年內，那個小鎮變成了熱鬧的城市。

ph.ex: The game was hard; we still won, however.
ph.exzh: 比賽很難；然而我們還是贏了。
