a.title: The Fastest Cat on Land
text: December 4 is International Cheetah Day. Cheetahs are the fastest animals on land.
A cheetah can run about 100 kilometres per hour. That is as fast as a car on the highway!
But a cheetah cannot run fast for a long time. After about 30 seconds, it must stop and rest.
Cheetahs have black lines under their eyes. These lines help them see in the bright sun.
Today, there are only about 7,000 cheetahs in the wild. They are losing their homes, and some farmers hurt them to protect their animals.
People in Africa are now using big dogs to keep farm animals safe, so farmers and cheetahs can live together.
tz: 12 月 4 日是國際獵豹日。獵豹是陸地上跑得最快的動物。
獵豹每小時大約可以跑 100 公里，跟高速公路上的汽車一樣快！
但是獵豹沒辦法長時間快跑。大約跑 30 秒後，牠就得停下來休息。
獵豹眼睛下方有黑色的線條，這些線條幫助牠們在強烈陽光下看清楚。
如今，野外只剩下大約 7,000 隻獵豹。牠們正在失去家園，有些農夫為了保護自己的牲畜而傷害牠們。
現在非洲的人們用大型犬來保護農場動物，讓農夫和獵豹可以一起生活。

b.title: Built for Speed, Running Out of Space
text: International Cheetah Day, held on December 4, was started by the scientist Laurie Marker, founder of the Cheetah Conservation Fund in Namibia. She chose the birthday of Khayam, a cheetah she had raised, to draw attention to the species.

Cheetahs are built for speed. Light bones, long legs and a flexible spine let them reach roughly 100 kilometres per hour in just a few seconds, while their long tail works like a rudder when they turn. However, they can only sprint for a short distance before they overheat.
Unlike lions, cheetahs cannot roar; instead they purr, chirp and hiss.

Today fewer than 7,000 adult cheetahs remain in the wild, mostly in southern and eastern Africa, with a tiny population surviving in Iran. They need huge areas to hunt, so habitat loss hits them hard, and many are killed by farmers protecting livestock.

Conservationists in Namibia give farmers large guard dogs that scare cheetahs away from goats and sheep, an approach that has reduced the number of cheetahs killed. Smuggling of cubs as pets remains a serious threat.
tz: 每年 12 月 4 日的國際獵豹日，是由納米比亞獵豹保育基金會創辦人、科學家蘿莉・馬克所發起。她選擇自己養大的獵豹卡雅姆的生日，來喚起大家對這個物種的關注。
獵豹天生為速度而生。輕盈的骨骼、修長的腿和柔軟的脊椎，讓牠們在短短幾秒內就能加速到每小時約 100 公里；轉彎時，長尾巴就像船舵一樣。然而，牠們只能衝刺一小段距離，否則身體會過熱。
和獅子不同，獵豹不會吼叫；牠們會發出呼嚕聲、啾啾聲和嘶嘶聲。
如今野外只剩不到 7,000 隻成年獵豹，大多在非洲南部和東部，伊朗也還殘存一個極小的族群。牠們需要非常大的範圍才能狩獵，所以棲地流失對牠們打擊很大，還有許多獵豹被保護牲畜的農夫殺死。
納米比亞的保育人士送給農夫大型護衛犬，把獵豹從山羊和綿羊身邊嚇走，這個方法已經減少了被殺的獵豹數量。把幼豹走私當寵物，仍是嚴重的威脅。

t: Cheetahs are built for speed.
Unlike lions, cheetahs cannot roar; instead they purr, chirp and hiss.
Today fewer than 7,000 adult cheetahs remain in the wild, mostly in southern and eastern Africa, with a tiny population surviving in Iran.
st.c: Conservationists in Namibia give farmers large guard dogs that scare cheetahs away from goats and sheep, an approach that has reduced the number of cheetahs killed.

c.title: The Price of Speed
text: The cheetah is evolution's sprinter, an animal so specialised for acceleration that its strengths double as weaknesses. International Cheetah Day, marked on December 4, draws attention to what that specialisation now costs.

Everything about the cheetah serves a few seconds of explosive pursuit: a lightweight frame, oversized nostrils and lungs, semi-retractable claws that grip like running spikes, and a tail that steers at speed. Yet the same lightness leaves it unable to defend its kills from lions and hyenas, and a chase lasting more than a few hundred metres risks dangerous overheating.

Above all, cheetahs need space. Because they hunt over vast ranges, often outside protected areas, they come into conflict with farmers. Their numbers have collapsed to fewer than 7,000 adults, and the Asiatic population survives only in Iran, in dangerously small numbers.

Some of the most promising conservation has been practical rather than glamorous. In Namibia, livestock guarding dogs have reduced the losses that once led farmers to shoot cheetahs on sight, showing that coexistence can be engineered.
Bolder schemes, such as relocating African cheetahs to India since 2022, remain controversial, a reminder that saving a specialist means restoring the wide, connected landscapes it evolved to cross.
tz: 獵豹是演化打造的短跑選手，為了加速而高度特化，以致於牠的長處同時也是弱點。每年 12 月 4 日的國際獵豹日，讓人注意到這種特化如今所付出的代價。
獵豹的一切都為了短短幾秒的爆發式追逐：輕盈的骨架、特大的鼻孔與肺、像釘鞋一樣抓地的半伸縮爪，以及能在高速中掌控方向的尾巴。然而，同樣的輕盈讓牠無法從獅子和鬣狗手中守住獵物，而追逐一旦超過幾百公尺，就可能危險地過熱。
最重要的是，獵豹需要空間。因為牠們在廣大的範圍內狩獵、常常跑出保護區，於是與農夫發生衝突。牠們的數量已崩跌到不到 7,000 隻成年個體，亞洲獵豹族群只殘存在伊朗，數量少得危險。
有些最有希望的保育工作，靠的是務實而非光鮮。在納米比亞，牲畜護衛犬減少了損失——過去農夫正是因為這些損失，一看到獵豹就開槍——證明共存是可以設計出來的。
更大膽的計畫，例如自 2022 年起把非洲獵豹遷移到印度，至今仍有爭議。這提醒我們：要拯救一個高度特化的物種，就必須恢復牠演化來穿越的那些廣闊、相連的土地。

ph.ex: Above all, be kind to your classmates.
ph.exzh: 最重要的是，要善待同學。

a.title: Helping Without Pay
text: December 5 is International Volunteer Day. A volunteer is a person who helps others without getting money.
Volunteers do many kinds of jobs. Some read books to children. Some clean beaches. Some help old people or animals.
In Taiwan, many students volunteer at libraries, hospitals and beach clean-ups.
Volunteering helps other people, but it also helps the volunteers. They make new friends, learn new skills and feel happy.
You do not need to be an adult to volunteer. Even a small job, like picking up trash in your park, makes a difference.
What could you do to help your community?
tz: 12 月 5 日是國際志工日。志工是不拿錢、主動幫助別人的人。
志工做很多種工作。有些人念書給小朋友聽，有些人清理海灘，有些人照顧老人或動物。
在台灣，很多學生會到圖書館、醫院當志工，或參加淨灘。
當志工能幫助別人，也能幫助志工自己。他們會交到新朋友、學到新技能，也覺得很快樂。
你不需要是大人才能當志工。就算是小小的工作，像是撿起公園裡的垃圾，也能帶來改變。
你可以為你的社區做些什麼呢？

b.title: Why Giving Time Matters
text: The United Nations created International Volunteer Day in 1985 to celebrate the millions of people who give their time to help others. It is marked every year on December 5.

Volunteers support communities in countless ways: tutoring children, caring for the elderly, rescuing animals, cleaning coastlines and responding to disasters. During emergencies, local volunteers are often the first to arrive and the last to leave.

Research suggests that volunteering can also benefit volunteers themselves. People who volunteer regularly often report feeling more connected and less stressed, and they gain practical skills such as teamwork and communication.
In Taiwan, many young people volunteer through schools, temples, hospitals and environmental groups, and some schools encourage students to record their service hours.
However, experts warn that good intentions are not enough. Effective volunteering means listening to what a community actually needs, rather than doing what volunteers assume will help.
tz: 聯合國在 1985 年設立國際志工日，表揚數百萬名付出時間幫助別人的人。這個日子每年都在 12 月 5 日。
志工以無數方式支持社區：輔導孩童課業、照顧長者、救援動物、清理海岸，以及投入救災。發生緊急狀況時，當地志工往往最先抵達、最後離開。
研究顯示，當志工也可能對志工本身有益。經常當志工的人常表示感覺和他人更有連結、壓力也比較小，還能學到團隊合作和溝通等實用技能。
在台灣，許多年輕人透過學校、寺廟、醫院和環保團體當志工，有些學校也鼓勵學生記錄服務時數。
不過，專家提醒，光有好意是不夠的。有效的志願服務，代表要傾聽社區真正需要什麼，而不是做志工自以為有幫助的事。

ph.ex: My mom gives her time to the school library every Friday.

ph.p: the first to arrive and the last to leave

ph.ex: Ask what your friend needs rather than guessing.
ph.exzh: 問問朋友需要什麼，而不是用猜的。

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?

Good intentions are always enough, so volunteers should simply do whatever they think helps.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：幫助社區、自己也受益、好的服務從傾聽開始。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?

q.q: Why are local volunteers “the first to arrive” in emergencies?

tr.en: During emergencies, local volunteers are often the first to arrive and the last to leave.

t: Volunteers support communities in countless ways: tutoring children, caring for the elderly, rescuing animals, cleaning coastlines and responding to disasters.
Research suggests that volunteering can also benefit volunteers themselves.
In Taiwan, many young people volunteer through schools, temples, hospitals and environmental groups, and some schools encourage students to record their service hours.
st.c: Effective volunteering means listening to what a community actually needs, rather than doing what volunteers assume will help.

c.title: The Ethics of Helping
text: Volunteering is usually celebrated as pure generosity, and International Volunteer Day, proclaimed by the United Nations in 1985 and held each December 5, rightly honours the vast unpaid labour that holds communities together.

Its scale is easy to underestimate. Volunteers staff food banks, tutor struggling students, answer crisis hotlines and, after earthquakes and typhoons, dig, cook and comfort long before outside help arrives. Much of the world's care work is done this way, quietly and without pay.

Volunteering also tends to reward those who give. Studies associate regular volunteering with stronger social ties and better wellbeing, though it is hard to tell how far helping causes happiness and how far happier people simply volunteer more.

Yet goodwill is not the same as good help. Critics of so-called 'voluntourism' point to short trips in which visitors build schools that local workers could have built better, or take photos with vulnerable children, meeting the volunteer's needs more than the community's.
The most effective volunteering is therefore humble: it asks before acting, commits for the long term, and measures success by what the community gains rather than by how the helper feels.
tz: 志願服務通常被讚頌為純粹的慷慨。聯合國於 1985 年宣布、每年 12 月 5 日舉行的國際志工日，正當地表彰了把社區凝聚在一起的大量無償勞動。
它的規模很容易被低估。志工在食物銀行值班、輔導學習困難的學生、接聽危機熱線；地震和颱風過後，早在外部援助抵達前，他們就已經在挖掘、煮飯和安慰災民。世界上大量的照護工作，就是這樣安靜、無償地完成的。
志願服務也常常回饋付出的人。研究把規律當志工與更緊密的人際關係、更好的身心狀態聯想在一起，不過很難分辨究竟是助人帶來快樂，還是快樂的人本來就比較常當志工。
然而，善意不等於好的幫助。批評所謂「志工旅遊」的人指出，有些短期旅程中，訪客蓋的學校，當地工人其實可以蓋得更好；或者訪客和弱勢兒童合照——滿足的是志工的需求，多過社區的需求。
因此，最有效的志願服務是謙卑的：先詢問再行動、長期投入，並以社區得到什麼、而不是助人者感覺如何，來衡量成功。

ph.ex: Shared jokes hold our class together.
ph.exzh: 共同的笑話讓我們班凝聚在一起。

ph.ex: She finished her project long before the deadline.
ph.exzh: 她早在截止日前就完成了專題。

ph.ex: Being busy is not the same as being productive.
ph.exzh: 忙碌不等於有效率。

ph.ex: Teachers point to sleep as a key to good grades.
ph.exzh: 老師指出睡眠是好成績的關鍵。

ph.ex: Learning a language is a plan for the long term.
ph.exzh: 學語言是一個長期的計畫。

ph.ex: Choose clubs you enjoy rather than ones your friends choose.
ph.exzh: 選你喜歡的社團，而不是朋友選的。

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Volunteering is always pure generosity, so any kind of help is equally good for every community.
Voluntourism is the most effective way to help, because short trips bring nice photos and new schools.
People who volunteer are proven to be happier, which is the main reason to volunteer at all.
Volunteering is valuable, but the best help is humble and long-term, focused on what communities need.
q.why: 主旨：志願服務有價值，但最好的幫助是謙卑、長期、以需求為本。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “vulnerable” describes children who are ___.
opts: very wealthy and famous
easily harmed and in need of protection
very good at building new schools in poor areas
volunteers themselves
q.why: vulnerable = 弱勢、易受傷害的。

q.q: Why is it “hard to tell” whether helping causes happiness?
opts: Happier people may simply volunteer more in the first place
Volunteers never report their feelings
Studies about volunteering and happiness do not exist yet
Happiness cannot be measured at all
q.why: 第三段：也可能是快樂的人比較常當志工。

q.q: What is the writer's attitude toward 'voluntourism'?
opts: Enthusiastic, as the best and most useful form of help in the world
Neutral, with no opinion given
Critical, because it may serve visitors more than communities
Confused about what it means
q.why: 第四段：meeting the volunteer's needs more than the community's。

q.q: What is the function of “Yet” at the start of paragraph 4?
opts: To add another benefit
To introduce a new date
To summarise the whole essay and repeat the main benefits of volunteering
To turn from the benefits of volunteering to its possible problems
q.why: Yet 轉向志願服務可能的問題。

q.q: Two volunteer plans: (A) a one-week trip to paint a school and take photos; (B) a year of weekly online tutoring that a village asked for. Which fits the essay's advice?
opts: Plan B, because it was requested and is long-term
Plan A, because it is quick and makes nice photos
Both are exactly equal in value
Neither, because volunteering never helps
q.why: 最後一段：asks before acting, commits for the long term。

st.m: The most effective volunteering is therefore humble: it asks before acting, commits for the long term, and measures success by what the community gains rather than by how the helper feels.
st.mz: 最有效的志工服務是謙虛的：先詢問再行動、長期投入，並用對方的需要來衡量成果。
t: Its scale is easy to underestimate.
Volunteering also tends to reward those who give.
Yet goodwill is not the same as good help.
st.c: The most effective volunteering is therefore humble: it asks before acting, commits for the long term, and measures success by what the community gains rather than by how the helper feels.

discuss: Have you ever volunteered or helped someone without being paid? How did it feel?
What does your school or community need most? How could students help?
Is it better to help a lot for one day, or a little every week for a long time? Why?

topic: St Nicholas Day: Where Santa Claus Came From
zh: 聖尼古拉節：聖誕老人從哪裡來？
src: Smithsonian · BBC · The New York Times

a.title: The Kind Man Behind Santa
text: December 6 is St Nicholas Day. In some countries in Europe, children put out their shoes the night before. In the morning, they find sweets and small gifts inside!
St Nicholas was a real man. He lived about 1,700 years ago in a town that is now in Turkey.
People say he was very kind and liked to give gifts in secret.
In one old story, he dropped bags of gold through a window at night to help a poor family.
Later, people from the Netherlands took the story of 'Sinterklaas' to America. Over time, he became Santa Claus.
Today, Santa Claus is famous all over the world, but his story began with a kind man who helped others.
tz: 12 月 6 日是聖尼古拉節。在歐洲的一些國家，孩子們會在前一晚把鞋子放在外面。到了早上，他們會在鞋子裡發現糖果和小禮物！
聖尼古拉是真實存在的人。他大約生活在 1,700 年前，住在一個現今屬於土耳其的小鎮。
人們說他非常善良，喜歡偷偷送禮物。
在一個古老的故事裡，他在晚上把一袋袋金子從窗戶丟進去，幫助一個貧窮的家庭。
後來，荷蘭人把「辛特克拉斯」的故事帶到了美國。久而久之，他就變成了聖誕老人。
如今，聖誕老人在全世界都很有名，但他的故事，是從一個幫助別人的善良男人開始的。

ph.ex: Please put out the plates for dinner.
ph.exzh: 請把晚餐的盤子擺出來。

ph.ex: We planned a birthday party for our teacher in secret.
ph.exzh: 我們偷偷幫老師籌備生日派對。

ph.ex: Over time, my English got better.
ph.exzh: 久而久之，我的英文進步了。

ph.ex: I always pack my bag the night before a trip.
ph.exzh: 我總是在旅行前一晚整理包包。

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: St Nicholas and how his story became Santa Claus
How to put sweets inside your shoes
Why the Netherlands is so close to Turkey on the map
How to find gold in an old town
q.why: 全文介紹聖尼古拉如何演變成聖誕老人。

q.q: According to the reading, which is TRUE?
opts: St Nicholas was a man from a story who never really lived.
St Nicholas lived in a town that is now in Turkey.
Children in Europe put out their socks on Christmas Day.
St Nicholas liked to give gifts in front of many people.
q.why: 第 2 段：He lived … in a town that is now in Turkey。他是真實人物；孩子是在前一晚放「鞋子」；他喜歡「偷偷」送禮。

q.q: Which is the right order? (a) He became Santa Claus. (b) He gave gold to a poor family. (c) People took the story to America.
q.why: 送金子給窮人家（第 4 段）→ 荷蘭人把故事帶到美國（第 5 段）→ 漸漸變成聖誕老人（第 5 段）。

q.q: In the text, “in secret” means ___.
opts: in front of everyone you know
in a big box
without other people knowing
at a party
q.why: in secret = 秘密地。

q.q: Why did St Nicholas drop gold through the window?
opts: To play a game
To help a poor family
To hide his money
To buy a new house
q.why: 第四段：to help a poor family。

q.q: Your class wants to celebrate St Nicholas Day in his spirit. Which idea fits best?
opts: Ask everyone in your class to buy you expensive presents
Hide all the shoes in the classroom
Secretly leave kind notes or small gifts for classmates
Only celebrate if Santa visits school
q.why: 故事重點：善良、偷偷送禮。

gt.en: St Nicholas was a real man.
gt.zh: 聖尼古拉是真實存在的人。

gt.en: People say he was very kind and liked to give gifts in secret.
gt.zh: 人們說他非常善良，喜歡偷偷送禮物。

gt.en: Over time, he became Santa Claus.
gt.zh: 久而久之，他變成了聖誕老人。

gt.en: Today, Santa Claus is famous all over the world, but his story began with a kind man who helped others.
gt.zh: 如今聖誕老人全世界有名，但他的故事是從一個幫助別人的善良男人開始的。

st.m: Today, Santa Claus is famous all over the world, but his story began with a kind man who helped others.
st.mz: 聖誕老人的故事源自一位喜歡偷偷送禮、幫助別人的好人：聖尼古拉。
t: St Nicholas was a real man.
People say he was very kind and liked to give gifts in secret.
In one old story, he dropped bags of gold through a window at night to help a poor family.
Later, people from the Netherlands took the story of 'Sinterklaas' to America.
st.c: Today, Santa Claus is famous all over the world, but his story began with a kind man who helped others.

b.title: From Bishop to Santa
text: Long before Santa Claus flew through the sky, there was Nicholas, a fourth-century bishop of Myra, a town in what is now Turkey. December 6, the date traditionally given for his death, became his feast day.

Nicholas was famous for his generosity. In the best-known legend, he secretly threw bags of gold into the home of a poor man who could not afford dowries for his three daughters. Some versions say the gold landed in stockings drying by the fire, which may explain why children still hang up stockings.
In the Netherlands, the saint became Sinterklaas, who arrives in November and leaves gifts in children's shoes on December 5 or 6.

Dutch settlers carried the tradition to New York, where writers and artists gradually transformed him. An 1823 poem, now known as 'The Night Before Christmas', gave him a sleigh and reindeer, and the cartoonist Thomas Nast later added his North Pole workshop.
Contrary to a popular myth, a soft-drink company did not invent Santa's red suit, though its advertisements from the 1930s helped make that image famous worldwide.
tz: 早在聖誕老人飛越天空之前，就有尼古拉——一位四世紀時米拉城的主教，米拉位於今天的土耳其。12 月 6 日傳統上被認為是他過世的日子，後來成了他的節日。
尼古拉以慷慨聞名。在最有名的傳說中，有一位窮人付不出三個女兒的嫁妝，尼古拉便偷偷把一袋袋金子丟進他家。有些版本說，金子正好掉進在火爐邊晾乾的長襪裡——這或許能解釋為什麼孩子們至今仍會掛起長襪。
在荷蘭，這位聖人變成了辛特克拉斯，他在 11 月抵達，並在 12 月 5 日或 6 日把禮物放進孩子們的鞋子裡。
荷蘭移民把這個傳統帶到了紐約，作家和藝術家在那裡逐漸改造了他的形象。一首 1823 年的詩——如今被稱為〈聖誕前夜〉——讓他有了雪橇和馴鹿，漫畫家湯瑪斯・奈斯特後來又加上他在北極的工作坊。
和一個流行的迷思相反，聖誕老人的紅色外套並不是某家汽水公司發明的，不過該公司 1930 年代的廣告，確實讓這個形象紅遍全世界。

ph.ex: Tainan is famous for its delicious snacks.
ph.exzh: 台南以美味小吃聞名。

ph.ex: I can't afford a new phone this year.
ph.exzh: 我今年買不起新手機。

ph.ex: Hang up your jacket when you get home.
ph.exzh: 回到家要把外套掛起來。

ph.ex: Contrary to what many think, cats can be very friendly.
ph.exzh: 和很多人想的相反，貓也可以很親人。

ph.ex: People drank tea long before coffee became popular here.
ph.exzh: 早在咖啡流行之前，這裡的人就喝茶了。

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: A soft-drink company invented Santa Claus and his famous red suit in the 1930s to sell more of its drinks.
Sinterklaas lives at the North Pole and arrives in New York every year in November.
Thomas Nast was a bishop in Myra who wrote 'The Night Before Christmas' in 1823.
The generous fourth-century bishop Nicholas slowly became today's Santa Claus through traditions and stories.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：慷慨的主教經由傳統與故事演變成聖誕老人。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: A soft-drink company invented Santa's red suit in the 1930s.
Thomas Nast gave Santa his sleigh and his reindeer.
A poem from 1823 gave the saint a sleigh and reindeer.
Sinterklaas leaves gifts in children's stockings in November.
q.why: 第 4 段：An 1823 poem … gave him a sleigh and reindeer。飲料公司「沒有」發明紅衣；Nast 加的是北極工坊；Sinterklaas 是在 12 月 5 或 6 日把禮物放在「鞋子」裡。

q.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 5?
opts: To correct a popular belief about Santa's red suit
To explain how Nicholas secretly helped a poor family
To describe the North Pole workshop in detail
To praise a company for creating Santa Claus
q.why: 第 5 段 Contrary to a popular myth——糾正「紅衣是飲料公司發明的」這個流行說法。

q.q: In paragraph 1, a “bishop” is ___.
opts: a person who makes toys for children
a senior leader in the Christian church
a kind of sleigh
a poor farmer
q.why: bishop = 主教。

q.q: What might explain why children hang up stockings?
opts: Stockings are much easier to fill with gifts than shoes are
Thomas Nast drew stockings in 1823
The soft-drink company sold stockings
A legend says Nicholas's gold landed in stockings by the fire
q.why: 第二段：which may explain why children still hang up stockings。

q.q: A friend says: “Santa's red suit was invented by a soft-drink company.” Based on the text, what is the best reply?
opts: True: the soft-drink company created Santa Claus in the 1930s for its advertisements
True: Thomas Nast worked for the company
Not true: the company's ads made the image famous, but did not invent it
Not true: Santa has always worn green
q.why: 第五段：did not invent … though its advertisements … helped make that image famous。

tr.en: Nicholas was famous for his generosity.
tr.zh: 尼古拉以慷慨聞名。

tr.en: Dutch settlers carried the tradition to New York, where writers and artists gradually transformed him.
tr.zh: 荷蘭移民把這個傳統帶到紐約，作家和藝術家在那裡逐漸改造了他的形象。

tr.en: In the Netherlands, the saint became Sinterklaas, who arrives in November and leaves gifts in children's shoes on December 5 or 6.
tr.zh: 在荷蘭，這位聖人變成了辛特克拉斯，他在 11 月抵達，並在 12 月 5 日或 6 日把禮物放進孩子的鞋子裡。

st.m: Long before Santa Claus flew through the sky, there was Nicholas, a fourth-century bishop of Myra, a town in what is now Turkey.
st.mz: 聖誕老人源自四世紀的主教聖尼古拉，經過荷蘭與美國的傳統，演變成今天的模樣。
t: Nicholas was famous for his generosity.
In the Netherlands, the saint became Sinterklaas, who arrives in November and leaves gifts in children's shoes on December 5 or 6.
Dutch settlers carried the tradition to New York, where writers and artists gradually transformed him.
st.c: Contrary to a popular myth, a soft-drink company did not invent Santa's red suit, though its advertisements from the 1930s helped make that image famous worldwide.

c.title: How a Saint Became a Brand
text: Few figures have travelled as far as Nicholas of Myra. A fourth-century bishop in what is now Turkey, he left almost no reliable historical record, yet his feast day, December 6, seeded one of the most recognisable characters on Earth.

His reputation rested on stories of discreet generosity, above all the legend of gold tossed by night into the house of a man too poor to provide dowries for his daughters. The secrecy mattered: the gift was meant to spare the family shame, not to win the giver praise.

Over centuries the saint was absorbed into local customs, becoming the Dutch Sinterklaas, whom settlers carried to New York. There, nineteenth-century writers and illustrators remade him, supplying the sleigh, the reindeer and the North Pole, and turning a stern bishop into a jolly figure suited to a commercial Christmas.
The often-repeated claim that a soft-drink brand invented his red suit is false; red Santas long predate its famous 1930s advertisements, though those campaigns standardised the image globally.

The irony is hard to miss. A saint remembered for anonymous giving has become the face of the most intensely marketed season of the year, a reminder that traditions survive by changing, sometimes almost beyond recognition.
tz: 很少有人物能像米拉的尼古拉那樣「走」得這麼遠。這位四世紀的主教住在今天的土耳其，幾乎沒有留下可靠的歷史紀錄，然而他的節日——12 月 6 日——卻孕育出地球上最廣為人知的角色之一。
他的名聲建立在低調慷慨的故事上，其中最著名的是：一個窮到付不出女兒嫁妝的男人家中，夜裡被扔進了金子。保密很重要：這份禮物是為了讓那家人免於蒙羞，而不是為了替送禮者贏得讚美。
經過幾個世紀，這位聖人被融入各地習俗，成為荷蘭的辛特克拉斯，再由移民帶到紐約。在那裡，十九世紀的作家和插畫家重新塑造他，加上雪橇、馴鹿和北極，把一位嚴肅的主教變成適合商業化聖誕節的快活人物。
常被重複的「某汽水品牌發明了他的紅色外套」說法是錯的；紅衣聖誕老人遠早於該品牌著名的 1930 年代廣告，不過那些廣告確實讓這個形象在全球標準化。
諷刺之處顯而易見。一位以匿名贈與被紀念的聖人，成了一年中行銷最密集季節的代言人——提醒我們，傳統是靠改變而存活下來的，有時甚至變得幾乎認不出來。

ph.ex: Our team's success rests on good teamwork.
ph.exzh: 我們隊伍的成功建立在良好的團隊合作上。

ph.ex: Above all, remember to drink water during the race.
ph.exzh: 最重要的是，比賽中記得喝水。

ph.ex: The night market comes alive by night.
ph.exzh: 夜市在夜裡熱鬧起來。

ph.ex: The new red building is hard to miss.
ph.exzh: 那棟新的紅色建築很難不注意到。

ph.ex: My old school has changed almost beyond recognition.
ph.exzh: 我以前的學校幾乎變得認不出來了。

ph.ex: This book is suited to beginners.
ph.exzh: 這本書適合初學者。

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: Nicholas of Myra left detailed historical records, so we know exactly how Santa's modern image was first designed and spread around the world.
A soft-drink company invented Santa's red suit in the 1930s and created the whole Christmas tradition.
Sinterklaas and Santa Claus are completely unrelated figures from two different countries and times.
A saint known for quiet, secret giving was reshaped over centuries into a commercial symbol, showing how traditions survive by changing.
q.why: 主旨：低調送禮的聖人被改造成商業象徵——傳統靠改變而存活。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “discreet” means ___.
opts: very loud, public and proud in the town
expensive and showy
careful not to attract attention
strict and serious
q.why: discreet = 低調謹慎的。

q.q: Why does the writer say “The secrecy mattered”?
opts: Secret gifts are worth more money
The gift aimed to save the family from shame, not to earn praise
Nicholas was afraid of the family
The family wanted to stay hidden from everyone in the town all the time
q.why: 第二段：spare the family shame, not to win the giver praise。

q.q: How does the writer view the modern Santa compared with the original saint?
opts: With a sense of irony
With anger and disgust
With complete approval
With no opinion
q.why: 第五段：The irony is hard to miss。

q.q: What does paragraph 4 mainly do?
opts: Correct a popular myth about the red suit
Describe Nicholas's childhood and early life
List modern Christmas songs
Explain how reindeer fly
q.why: 第四段：糾正汽水品牌發明紅衣的迷思。

q.q: Which evidence would BEST disprove the claim that a soft-drink brand invented the red-suited Santa?
opts: A 1930s soft-drink advertisement showing Santa in red
A modern Christmas card with Santa in red
A survey of what children believe today
Pictures of red-suited Santas published before the 1930s
q.why: 第四段：red Santas long predate its 1930s advertisements——更早的圖片最能反駁。

st.m: Few figures have travelled as far as Nicholas of Myra.
st.mz: 以匿名送禮聞名的聖尼古拉，如今卻成了最商業化節日的代言人。
t: His reputation rested on stories of discreet generosity, above all the legend of gold tossed by night into the house of a man too poor to provide dowries for his daughters.
Over centuries the saint was absorbed into local customs, becoming the Dutch Sinterklaas, whom settlers carried to New York.
The often-repeated claim that a soft-drink brand invented his red suit is false; red Santas long predate its famous 1930s advertisements, though those campaigns standardised the image globally.
st.c: A saint remembered for anonymous giving has become the face of the most intensely marketed season of the year, a reminder that traditions survive by changing, sometimes almost beyond recognition.

discuss: St Nicholas gave gifts in secret. Why might giving secretly be kinder than giving in public?
How have holiday traditions changed in your family or in Taiwan over time?
Do you think Christmas today is too focused on shopping? Explain your view.

topic: World AIDS Day: Facts Over Fear
zh: 世界愛滋日：用事實取代恐懼
src: WHO · UNAIDS · NBC

a.title: The Red Ribbon
text: December 1 is World AIDS Day. On this day, many people wear a red ribbon.
HIV is a virus that attacks the body's defence system. Without medicine, it can cause a serious illness called AIDS.
Today there is no cure for HIV, but there is very good medicine. People with HIV who take their medicine every day can live long, healthy lives.
You cannot get HIV from hugging, shaking hands, or sharing a cup or a toilet.
In the past, many people were afraid of people with HIV and treated them badly. This is called stigma.
The red ribbon reminds us to learn the facts and to be kind.
tz: 12 月 1 日是世界愛滋日。這一天，許多人會戴上紅絲帶。
HIV（愛滋病毒）是一種會攻擊身體防禦系統的病毒。如果沒有藥物，它會造成一種叫做愛滋病（AIDS）的嚴重疾病。
現在 HIV 還沒有辦法治癒，但已經有非常好的藥物。感染 HIV 的人只要每天吃藥，就能長久、健康地生活。
擁抱、握手，或共用杯子、馬桶，都不會感染 HIV。
過去，很多人害怕感染 HIV 的人，還對他們很不友善。這叫做汙名。
紅絲帶提醒我們：要了解事實，也要待人友善。

ph.ex: My little sister is afraid of the dark.
ph.exzh: 我妹妹怕黑。

ph.ex: The players shake hands after every game.
ph.exzh: 球員每場比賽後都會握手。

ph.ex: In the past, people wrote letters instead of messages.
ph.exzh: 在過去，人們寫信而不是傳訊息。

ph.ex: It's wrong to treat new students badly.
ph.exzh: 對新同學不好是不對的。

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: How to make a red ribbon for a party
Why people should stop hugging each other in winter
How medicine is made in hospitals
World AIDS Day, the facts about HIV, and being kind
q.why: 全文介紹世界愛滋日、HIV 的事實與友善待人。

q.q: According to the reading, which is TRUE?
opts: Doctors now have a medicine that can completely cure HIV.
People with HIV can live long lives if they take medicine.
You can get HIV by sharing a cup with someone.
World AIDS Day is on December 11 every year.
q.why: 第 3 段：People with HIV who take their medicine every day can live long, healthy lives。目前沒有治癒的藥；共用杯子不會傳染；日期是 12 月 1 日。

q.q: In paragraph 5, what does "This" in "This is called stigma" refer to?
opts: treating people with HIV badly
taking medicine every single day
wearing a red ribbon
learning the facts
q.why: This 指前一句：人們害怕感染者並且不好好對待他們——這就叫污名。

q.q: In the text, “stigma” means ___.
opts: a kind of red ribbon
a type of medicine
treating people badly because of fear
a special hospital for sick animals
q.why: 第五段：treated them badly. This is called stigma。

q.q: What can people with HIV do to stay healthy?
opts: Stop shaking hands with friends
Take their medicine every day
Wear a red ribbon every day
Stay away from all people
q.why: 第三段。

q.q: A classmate says, “Don't share a cup with him — he might have HIV.” Based on the text, what is the kindest and most correct reply?
opts: You're right, we should all stay far away from him so that we don't get sick
Let's ask him to wear a red ribbon
You can't get HIV from sharing a cup, so let's not leave him out
Let's tell the teacher to move him
q.why: 第四、五段：共用杯子不會感染，排擠就是汙名。

gt.en: On this day, many people wear a red ribbon.
gt.zh: 這一天，許多人會戴上紅絲帶。

gt.en: HIV is a virus that attacks the body's defence system.

st.mz: 紅絲帶提醒我們要了解愛滋病的正確知識，並且友善對待感染者。

b.title: Living With HIV Today
text: World AIDS Day has been held every December 1 since 1988, making it the first global day dedicated to a single health issue. Its symbol, the red ribbon, stands for awareness and support.

HIV, the human immunodeficiency virus, weakens the immune system. Untreated, it can lead to AIDS, which allows dangerous infections to take hold. In the 1980s and 1990s, millions of people died, and fear spread almost as fast as the virus.

Science has transformed that picture. Antiretroviral medicines do not cure HIV, but they control it so well that people who start treatment early can expect a nearly normal lifespan. Moreover, people whose treatment keeps the virus at undetectable levels cannot pass it on to sexual partners, a finding summed up as 'Undetectable = Untransmittable'.
Around 40 million people live with HIV worldwide, and many still cannot get treatment.
Experts say one of the biggest barriers is stigma. People who fear being judged may avoid getting tested, so accurate knowledge and kindness are part of the cure.
tz: 自 1988 年起，每年 12 月 1 日都會舉辦世界愛滋日，這是第一個專門針對單一健康議題的全球紀念日。它的象徵紅絲帶，代表關注與支持。
HIV（人類免疫缺乏病毒）會削弱免疫系統。如果不治療，可能會發展成愛滋病，讓危險的感染趁虛而入。在 1980 和 1990 年代，有數百萬人死亡，恐懼幾乎和病毒擴散得一樣快。
科學已經徹底改變了這個局面。抗反轉錄病毒藥物雖然無法治癒 HIV，卻能把它控制得非常好，及早開始治療的人可以預期擁有接近一般人的壽命。此外，若治療讓病毒維持在測不到的程度，就不會經由性行為傳給伴侶——這項發現被總結為「測不到＝不具傳染力（U=U）」。
全世界約有四千萬人帶著 HIV 生活，其中許多人仍然無法獲得治療。
專家表示，最大的障礙之一是汙名。害怕被評斷的人可能會避免去檢測，所以正確的知識與友善，也是治療的一部分。

ph.ex: The letters 'UN' stand for United Nations.
ph.exzh: 「UN」代表聯合國。

ph.ex: Too little sleep can lead to poor grades.
ph.exzh: 睡太少可能導致成績不好。

ph.ex: Once a bad habit takes hold, it is hard to stop.
ph.exzh: 壞習慣一旦扎根，就很難改掉。

ph.ex: The plan is cheap. Moreover, it is easy to do.
ph.exzh: 這個計畫很便宜，此外也很容易做到。

ph.ex: Please pass this message on to your parents.
ph.exzh: 請把這個訊息轉告你的父母。

ph.ex: Can you sum up the story in one sentence?
ph.exzh: 你可以用一句話總結這個故事嗎？

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: HIV can now be fully cured, so World AIDS Day is mainly a celebration of the past.
Treatment now lets people with HIV live long lives, but stigma and lack of access still stand in the way.
World AIDS Day was started in 1988 to sell red ribbons to people around the world.
Fear of HIV is helpful, because it makes people much more careful and more likely to get tested in the end.
q.why: 涵蓋全文：治療讓人長壽，但汙名與取得治療的困難仍是障礙。

q.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
opts: Antiretroviral medicines can cure HIV if people start them early.
About 4 million people live with HIV around the world.
The red ribbon stands for danger and warning.
World AIDS Day was the first global day for one health issue.
q.why: 第 1 段：the first global day dedicated to a single health issue。藥物能控制但「不能治癒」；約 4,000 萬人；紅絲帶代表關懷與支持。

q.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 3?
opts: To show how science has changed life with HIV
To describe the deaths of the 1980s and 1990s
To explain why people avoid getting tested
To introduce the meaning of the red ribbon
q.why: 第 3 段 Science has transformed that picture——說明藥物讓感染者能接近正常壽命、也不會傳給伴侶。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “lifespan” means ___.
opts: how fast a virus spreads
the size of a hospital
how long a person lives
the cost of medicine
q.why: lifespan = 壽命。

q.q: Why can stigma make the HIV problem worse?
opts: Stigma makes medicine stop working
People afraid of being judged may avoid getting tested
Stigma makes the virus spread more easily through the air
Stigma lowers the number of doctors
q.why: 第五段：may avoid getting tested。

q.q: A social media post says: “HIV is a death sentence, so don't bother getting tested.” Based on the text, what is wrong with it?
opts: With early treatment, people can expect a nearly normal lifespan, so testing matters
Nothing, it matches what the text says
HIV can be cured with one pill
Testing for HIV is not available anywhere in the world yet, even in big hospitals
q.why: 第三段：及早治療可接近正常壽命——檢測很重要。

c.title: From Death Sentence to Manageable Condition
text: When World AIDS Day was first observed on December 1, 1988, an HIV diagnosis was widely understood as a death sentence. The disease was spreading rapidly, treatment was primitive, and fear and prejudice shaped public responses as much as science did.

Few medical turnarounds have been as dramatic. Combination antiretroviral therapy, introduced in the mid-1990s, converted HIV from a fatal illness into a chronic, manageable condition. Today a person diagnosed early and treated consistently can expect to live almost as long as anyone else.

Treatment also became prevention. Large studies established that people whose viral load is suppressed to undetectable levels do not transmit the virus sexually, a finding that reframed people living with HIV not as dangers to be avoided but as partners in ending the epidemic.

Yet the turnaround is unevenly shared. Of roughly 40 million people living with HIV, millions still lack treatment, and new infections continue, particularly among young people and marginalised groups.

The most stubborn obstacle may be social rather than medical. Stigma discourages testing and treatment; scientific progress therefore depends, in the end, on whether societies replace fear with facts.
tz: 1988 年 12 月 1 日第一次舉辦世界愛滋日時，診斷出 HIV 普遍被視為被判了死刑。疾病快速蔓延，治療方式很原始，而恐懼和偏見對社會反應的影響，不亞於科學。
很少有醫學上的大逆轉像這樣戲劇化。1990 年代中期推出的雞尾酒式抗反轉錄病毒療法，把 HIV 從致命疾病轉變為可以控制的慢性病。如今，及早診斷並持續治療的人，可以預期活得幾乎和其他人一樣久。
治療也成了預防。大型研究證實，病毒量被抑制到測不到程度的人，不會經由性行為傳染病毒——這項發現重新定義了感染者：他們不是需要避開的危險，而是終結這場流行病的夥伴。
然而，這場大逆轉的成果分配並不均。在大約四千萬名感染者中，仍有數百萬人無法獲得治療，新感染也持續發生，尤其是在年輕人和邊緣化族群之中。
最頑固的障礙，或許是社會性的，而不是醫學上的。汙名讓人不敢檢測和治療；因此，科學進步最終取決於社會能否以事實取代恐懼。

ph.ex: Your effort matters as much as your talent.
ph.exzh: 你的努力和天分一樣重要。

ph.m: not as dangers to be avoided but as partners
ph.ex: She sees mistakes not as failures but as lessons.
ph.exzh: 她不把錯誤看成失敗，而是當成學習。

ph.ex: In the end, we won the game by one point.
ph.exzh: 最後我們以一分之差贏了比賽。

ph.ex: Talk to your friend rather than ignoring the problem.
ph.exzh: 和朋友談談，而不是忽略問題。

ph.ex: Try to replace sugary drinks with water.
ph.exzh: 試著用水取代含糖飲料。

ph.ex: I like fruit, particularly mangoes.
ph.exzh: 我喜歡水果，尤其是芒果。

q.q: Which best captures the writer's argument?
opts: HIV remains a death sentence today, because no treatment has improved at all since World AIDS Day first began around the world.
Medicine has turned HIV into a manageable condition, but unequal access and stigma still decide whether the epidemic ends.
The main problem today is medical, since social attitudes toward HIV have already fully changed.
Treatment helps individuals but has no effect at all on preventing the virus from spreading.
q.why: 主旨：醫學讓 HIV 可控，但治療不均與汙名決定能否終結疫情。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “chronic” means ___.
opts: very sudden
completely cured
lasting a long time
easy to catch
q.why: chronic = 慢性的。

q.q: How did the 'treatment as prevention' finding change how people living with HIV are seen?
opts: From patients to doctors
From young people to old people who need more care in hospitals
From partners to strangers
From dangers to be avoided to partners in ending the epidemic
q.why: 第三段。

q.q: How does the writer describe progress against HIV?
opts: Dramatic but unevenly shared
Slow and disappointing everywhere
Complete and finished
Unimportant compared with fear
q.why: 第二、四段：dramatic … Yet … unevenly shared。

q.q: What does the final paragraph conclude?
opts: New medicines will make stigma disappear by themselves, without help
Progress ultimately depends on societies replacing fear with facts
Testing should be avoided
The epidemic has already ended
q.why: 結尾：depends … on whether societies replace fear with facts。

q.q: A school wants to support World AIDS Day. Which plan best follows the essay's conclusion?
opts: Run a lesson that gives accurate facts about HIV and challenges stigma
Hand out red ribbons without explaining anything about HIV or AIDS to students
Avoid the topic because it might make students afraid
Tell students that HIV can be caught from sharing desks
q.why: 最後一段：以事實取代恐懼、對抗汙名。

st.m: The most stubborn obstacle may be social rather than medical.
st.mz: 愛滋治療已有驚人的進展，但最頑固的障礙是社會汙名，而不是醫學。
t: Few medical turnarounds have been as dramatic.
Treatment also became prevention.
Yet the turnaround is unevenly shared.
